display_title: Simplify tuple shapes in SPMD windowed einsum loops.

head_commit.message:
Simplify tuple shapes in SPMD windowed einsum loops.

Simplify the loop-state tuple shapes produced by `SpmdPartitioner` when sinking inputs or moving users into windowed einsum `kWhile` loops.

In `SinkInputNodesIntoWindowedDotGeneralLoopOnContractingDimensions` and `MoveUsersIntoWindowedDotGeneralLoopOnNonContractingDimensions`, replace the old loop-state entry in-place with the first new operand (or a scalar zero constant when sinking nullary-only inputs) and append any remaining new operands and outputs directly to the `kWhile` state tuple instead of packing them into a nested sub-tuple. This avoids nested tuples while preserving the canonical 5-element loop tuple indices `(0..4)`.

display_title: PR #51053: Fix NULL pointer dereference in HloEvaluator when evaluating a literal-less kConstant instruction

head_commit.message:
PR #51053: Fix NULL pointer dereference in HloEvaluator when evaluating a literal-less kConstant instruction

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51053

## Summary / Root Cause
`HloInstruction::CreateFromProto` (xla/hlo/ir/hlo_instruction.cc) constructs
a literal-less `HloConstantInstruction` whenever a `kConstant`
`HloInstructionProto` has no `literal` field set — regardless of the
`prohibit_empty_literal` parameter, which currently only governs an
*existing-but-empty* literal, not an *entirely absent* one. This state is
meant only for tooling that intentionally drops an oversized constant's
literal when dumping a module (`HloConstantInstruction::HasLiteral()` /
`DropLiteral()`).

If such a module is later evaluated, it crashes:
`HloEvaluator::GetEvaluatedLiteralFor()` unconditionally calls
`HloInstruction::literal()` whenever `IsConstant()` is true, which
dereferences the null `literal_` (`std::shared_ptr<Literal>`), producing a
SIGSEGV.

Found via a libFuzzer + ASan/UBSan harness targeting the
`HloModuleProto` deserialize → `HloEvaluator::Evaluate` path. Minimal
trigger: a single `kConstant` instruction proto with no `literal` field.

## The Fix

1. `HloInstruction::CreateFromProto`: when a `kConstant` proto has no
   `literal` and `prohibit_empty_literal` is true (the default used by
   every evaluation-facing caller — `run_hlo_module`, PJRT executable
   loading, etc.), return `absl::InvalidArgumentError` instead of silently
   constructing a literal-less instruction. Callers that genuinely need the
   "literal dropped" dump-only representation can still get it by passing
   `prohibit_empty_literal=false`.
2. `HloEvaluator::GetEvaluatedLiteralFor()` and
   `HloEvaluator::ExtractEvaluatedLiteralFor()`: added a `CHECK(HasLiteral())`
   defense-in-depth guard, consistent with the existing
   `CHECK(literal != nullptr)` a few lines below it, so that if any other
   path ever constructs a literal-less constant, evaluation fails with a
   clear diagnostic instead of a raw null-pointer SEGV.

## Impact

Prevents a denial-of-service crash (CWE-476, null pointer dereference) when
evaluating a malformed or maliciously crafted `HloModuleProto` whose
constant instruction is missing its literal payload. This affects any
consumer that deserializes and evaluates/interprets an `HloModuleProto` not
produced by XLA's own trusted compilation pipeline (the HLO interpreter
backend, `run_hlo_module`, or constant-folding over a less-trusted module).

## Behavior change to note for reviewers

Any existing caller that loads a "literal-dropped" dump **with**
`prohibit_empty_literal=true` and only inspects structure/shapes (never
evaluates) will now get an error instead of a literal-less instruction. That
matches the flag's documented intent ("prohibit empty literal") and we
believe no in-tree caller relies on the previous silent-success behavior for
this exact combination, but flagging it explicitly since it's the one
observable behavior change.
Copybara import of the project:

Previously `AutotuneResult::GemmKey` and `GemmBackendConfig` only recorded the heuristic algorithm index for cuBLASLt GEMMs.

display_title: [XLA:BufferAssignment] Derive the OOM fallback chain from the algorithm, and split the last step into SPATIAL and TEMPORAL.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:BufferAssignment] Derive the OOM fallback chain from the algorithm, and split the last step into SPATIAL and TEMPORAL.

We have two flags: one enables fast buffer assignment with the fallback
(`--xla_tpu_buffer_assignment_enable_fast_merge_fallback`), and the other
specifies the buffer assignment algorithm (`--xla_tpu_buffer_assignment_algorithm`).

With the fallback enabled, the algorithm for AssignBuffersWithSequentialOrdering specified via `--xla_tpu_buffer_assignment_algorithm` is now the first one to try, and it defines the fallback chain. Previously, enabling the fallback led to not respecting `--xla_tpu_buffer_assignment_algorithm`.

The last step of the chain used DEFAULT (= BEST_OF_SPATIAL_TEMPORAL), which always runs the heap simulation twice. It is now split into SPATIAL and then TEMPORAL. Since the fallback keeps the assignment with the lowest memory usage for each memory space, reaching TEMPORAL gives the same result as BEST_OF_SPATIAL_TEMPORAL, but TEMPORAL is skipped if SPATIAL already fits.

The pairs below are (non-sequential, sequential) algorithms. Depending on `--xla_tpu_buffer_assignment_algorithm`:

* auto, FAST_MERGE: (FAST_MERGE, FAST_MERGE) → (FAST_MERGE, FAST_SPLIT) → (DEFAULT, SPATIAL) → (DEFAULT, TEMPORAL)
* FAST_SPLIT: (FAST_MERGE, FAST_SPLIT) → (DEFAULT, SPATIAL) → (DEFAULT, TEMPORAL)
* SPATIAL: (FAST_MERGE, SPATIAL) → (DEFAULT, SPATIAL) → (DEFAULT, TEMPORAL)
* TEMPORAL: (FAST_MERGE, TEMPORAL) → (DEFAULT, SPATIAL) → (DEFAULT, TEMPORAL)
* DEFAULT, BEST_OF_SPATIAL_TEMPORAL: (FAST_MERGE, X) → (DEFAULT, X)

Only the memory spaces that exceed their memory limit (on TPU, HBM) are reassigned by the fallback steps. The other memory spaces (e.g. VMEM) keep the first assignment, where FAST_MERGE and FAST_SPLIT are replaced with DEFAULT, as before.

If the fallback flag is **disabled**, we respect the specified algorithm, and
nothing changes.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 998557925

display_title: Compile estimated configs on the thread pool in ConfigAssigner

head_commit.message:
Compile estimated configs on the thread pool in ConfigAssigner

With `prefer_estimated_configs`, each instruction's estimated configs were
compiled serially on the calling thread.

Now we split the config assignment into 3 stages:
* Look up forced or cached config
* If applicable, get an estimated config <- now they are compiled in parallel
* Get a tuned (if autotuning) or a first compilable/default config (if not)

This is similar to what we've been doing already, just split into stages more explicitly. We need to trigger the tuned and fallback config getter from the main thread, since getting supported configs is not thread-safe.

display_title: Add HloComputation::HasCalledComputations() to skip leaf computation scans.

head_commit.message:
Add HloComputation::HasCalledComputations() to skip leaf computation scans.

Post-fusion XLA modules contain thousands of leaf fusion and reducer
computations that call no subcomputations, yet `CallGraph::Build`, `HloDCE`,
`MakeComputationPostOrder`, `RemoveUnusedComputations`,
`MakeEmbeddedComputationsList`, and `CollectivePipeliner` scan every
instruction in leaf computations looking for callees or `while` loops.

Expose `HloComputation::HasCalledComputations()` (backed by the existing
`callee_computations_` map) and combine it with
`HloInstruction::MightHaveCalledComputations()` on `instructions_with_info()`
to skip leaf computations in O(1) and skip non-calling opcodes without

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Add HloComputation::HasCalledComputations() to skip leaf computation scans.

head_commit.message:
Add HloComputation::HasCalledComputations() to skip leaf computation scans.

Post-fusion XLA modules contain thousands of leaf fusion and reducer
computations that call no subcomputations, yet `CallGraph::Build`, `HloDCE`,
`MakeComputationPostOrder`, `RemoveUnusedComputations`,
`MakeEmbeddedComputationsList`, and `CollectivePipeliner` scan every
instruction in leaf computations looking for callees or `while` loops.

Expose `HloComputation::HasCalledComputations()` (backed by the existing
`callee_computations_` map) and combine it with
`HloInstruction::MightHaveCalledComputations()` on `instructions_with_info()`
to skip leaf computations in O(1) and skip non-calling opcodes without
chasing instruction pointers.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add ScanRewriterTriton to the GPU compiler pipeline behind a flag.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add ScanRewriterTriton to the GPU compiler pipeline behind a flag.

Add the debug option `xla_gpu_experimental_enable_triton_scan` (default off). When it is set, `GpuCompiler` runs `ScanRewriterTriton` in `OptimizeHloPostLayoutAssignment` before `AssociativeScanRewriter`, so eligible associative `kScan` instructions become Triton scan fusions instead of reduce-window trees.

The rewriter only sets the fusion kind to `__triton`; the tiling is chosen later by `PriorityFusion`, `FusionBlockLevelRewriter` or the autotuner.

`GpuCompiler` only adds the rewriter on GPUs that Triton supports. A tiled scan computes one row per block, so scans with a dimension of at least 32768 also need at least 64 rows (`kMinRowsForLongScan`); otherwise the hierarchical scan of `AssociativeScanRewriter` is faster (crossover at 64 rows on H100 and 32 on B200). Shorter scans are faster with Triton at any batch size.

`CanTritonHandleScan` now rejects scans over any dimension other than the last one, for which the tiled Triton scan computes wrong results.

For a cumsum with an elementwise epilogue on f32[B, N], with B from 1 to 256 and N from 1024 to 262144, enabling the flag is never slower on H100 and B200. It is 1.05–2.9x (H100) and 1.06–2.8x (B200) faster for N < 32768, and up to 1.9x (H100) and 2.3x (B200) faster for N ≥ 32768 and B ≥ 64.

A top-p sampling mask (softmax, cumsum, compare and select) on f32[B, K] with B from 1 to 256 and K in {64, 128} compiles to a single Triton kernel: 1.3–1.5 µs instead of 3.3–4.5 µs on H100, and 2.5–3.1 µs instead of 5.9–8.4 µs on B200.

head_commit.message:
PR #48501: [ROCm] Add  `ProfileOptions.advanced_configuration` into the ROCm tracer (PR1)

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/48501

First of three PRs that add `ProfileOptions.advanced_configuration` support to the ROCm tracer: this PR, #48502 (the parser) and #48503 (the wiring). This one is groundwork and adds no new options.

- Move `RocmTracerOptions` from `rocm_tracer.h` to `rocm_tracer_utils.h`, which has no ROCm dependency, so host-only targets (the parser in #48502) can use it. `rocm_tracer.h` already includes `rocm_tracer_utils.h`, so existing code is unaffected.
- Replace `AnnotationMap::Clear()` with `Reset(max_annotation_strings)`, which clears the entries and sets the capacity under one lock. The capacity was a `const` 1M. `RocmTracer::Enable()` calls `Reset()` before it starts the rocprofiler context.
- `AnnotationMap::Add()` checks the capacity once per event, so an event's annotation, ROCTX range and scope range ID are stored together or not at all. Before, the event that filled the last slot kept its annotation but lost its scope range ID.
- `RocmTracerOptions::max_annotation_strings` is a `std::optional` with no default. `Enable()` returns `InvalidArgument` if it is unset; 0 retains nothing.
- `RocmTraceCollectorOptions` fields default to 0 instead of being indeterminate, and its `max_annotation_strings`, which was set but never read, is removed.
- `hlo_op_profiler_rocm` drops its unused `//xla/service:gpu_plugin` dep, which `dwyu` flags once this PR edits the target's source, and depends on `rocm_tracer_utils` directly. `HloOpProfiler` takes an injected runner, and every binary that links it gets the plugin through `xla_test` or `matmul_perf_table_gen`, so link inputs don't change. `hlo_op_profiler_cuda` and `hlo_op_profiler_stub` still list it and can be cleaned up separately.

**Behaviour change:** `GpuTracer` sessions now get the 4M annotation capacity that `GetRocmTracerOptions()` already requested; `Enable()` ignored it and used 1M. The cap counts distinct strings, so most workloads won't see a difference (CUPTI's default is 1M). `hlo_op_profiler_rocm` keeps 1M. #48502 adds `gpu_max_annotation_strings` to set another value.

🎯 Justification

The ROCm `GpuTracer` ignores `advanced_configuration`: it reads only `device_type()`, so any `gpu_*` key a user sets, or misspells, is silently dropped. The CUPTI backend parses the map, but a bad key fails `Start()`, and `ProfilerController` then skips `CollectData()`, so the user loses the GPU trace with only a log line. #48502 and #48503 instead report problems in `XSpace.errors`/`warnings` and keep tracing. They need `RocmTracerOptions` in a header without ROCm dependencies, and an annotation capacity that can be set per session; this PR provides both.

♻️ Cleanup, 🐛 Bug Fix

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Initialize ROCR blit kernels in RocmExecutor::Init

head_commit.message:
Initialize ROCR blit kernels in RocmExecutor::Init

On ROCm, hipModuleUnload unmaps a code object's virtual address range without flushing the GPU's virtually-indexed scalar data and instruction caches. When ROCR later lazily initializes its internal BlitKernel shaders on the first >1 MB code object load or hsa_memory_copy call, GpuAgent::AssembleShader can reuse that virtual address range via mmap and writes the shader via CPU memcpy without invalidating the code caches. The GPU then fetches stale cache lines from the unloaded module and faults.

Therefore this change triggers a 4-byte hsa_memory_copy during RocmExecutor::Init so that ROCR initializes its permanent BlitKernel shader pages before any dynamic module is loaded and unloaded. This is part of an effort to get rid of test flakes in the XLA AMD Instinct GPU presubmits.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1005398601

display_title: Ignore the optimized HLO module in XLA:GPU AOT golden verification

head_commit.message:
Ignore the optimized HLO module in XLA:GPU AOT golden verification

The optimized HLO embedded in GpuExecutableProto is documented as debug-only,
but nearly every compiler change rewrites it (shapes, instruction ids,
backend-config JSON, fingerprints), so golden verification keeps failing on
changes that leave the executable's runtime behavior intact. Thunks, program
shape, constant allocations and the module's runtime debug options are still
compared. Forward compatibility of emitted HLO and changed constant data are no
longer flagged by this check; loading old artifacts stays covered by the
BackwardsCompatibility suites.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Swap different-axis squeeze_dims and expand_dims in Triton

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Swap different-axis squeeze_dims and expand_dims in Triton

When an operand of `tt.expand_dims` already contains a unit dimension adjacent
to the expanded axis, `triton_xla.squeeze_dims` on the pre-existing unit axis
produces the same tensor type as the `tt.expand_dims` operand. Checking type
equality instead of axis equality cancels the two ops instead of swapping them,
which stops `squeeze_dims` from reaching upstream `xtile.extract` tiles and
drops the `tt.expand_dims` before `tt.broadcast`.

Only fold `squeeze_dims(expand_dims(x))` to `x` when the axes match or `x` is a
1D unit tensor that cannot be squeezed further; otherwise swap the two ops so
unit dimensions continue propagating upward.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Check operand tile sizes against the register limit before tiling

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Check operand tile sizes against the register limit before tiling

The register pre-check before `Tile()` looked only at root tiles and missed
e.g. the whole-row operand tiles of softmax-like reductions. Such candidates
were tiled and only then rejected by `DoesComputationFitInRegisters`.

Tile the fusion symbolically once per search, collect its register-resident
tiles (roots, fusion operands and iotas), and check each candidate by
evaluating their symbolic tile sizes.

head_commit.message:
PR #51286: [XLA:GPU] Enable topk_special_floats_test on ROCm by encoding a plain float total-order key

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51286

📝 Summary of Changes
`topk_special_floats_test` expects `+0` to rank above `-0`. On ROCm the large shapes are rewritten to rocprim, and rocprim's float radix sort treats `+0` and `-0` as equal, so the returned index is wrong. CUDA still uses the float key, and its existing skip stays.
**What we change:**
- `SortComputationAnalysis` records `is_total_order` (`compare->order() == ComparisonOrder::kTotal`).
- The key is encoded only when the device is ROCm, the key type has a negative zero, the comparator is a plain compare (`kDefaultOrder`, not the NumPy-order or weak-order pattern), and `order=TOTAL`. `OrderedIntegralFromFloat` bitcasts the key to a signed integer of the same width and XORs negative values with the signed maximum. This is the map `ComparisonExpander` uses. It is its own inverse, so `FloatFromOrderedIntegral` applies it again and bitcasts back to the float after the sort.
- F16 and BF16 keys become S16, F32 becomes S32, and F64 becomes S64. The keys-only kernel is `CubSortKeys` for `int16_t`, `int32_t`, or `int64_t`. Among float keys, pair sorts are rewritten only for F32, so an encoded pair key is S32, which the pair kernel already accepts.
- Which sorts are rewritten does not change. The deviceless scratch-size lookup is keyed by byte width, and that width is unchanged. The encode and decode add elementwise ops before and after the sort, only for ROCm total-order float sorts that are already rewritten to rocprim.
- The replacement is built in one place, as suggested in review. For non-NumPy sorts, custom-call element 0 is the sorted key (decoded when it was encoded) and element 1 is the values. `PairInOperandOrder` restores operand order when the key was operand 1. `UnpackResultPair` is removed. New instructions are created through the sort, so they keep its metadata.
- `FloatTotalOrder` checks the original keys-only case, `f32[1000]` descending: the rocprim key is S32 on ROCm and F32 on CUDA. `SortTotalOrder` covers f16, bf16, f32, and f64, both directions, on `[16,128]`, and compares the result with the interpreter. `FloatTotalOrderPairKeyAtOperand0` and `FloatTotalOrderPairKeyAtOperand1` check both operand orders with `AMDMI210DeviceInfo`. `FloatTotalOrderSpecialValues` executes +0, -0, both infinities, and both NaNs on ROCm and skips on CUDA.
- `topk_special_floats_test` is enabled on ROCm. The NVIDIA skip for batch == 1, n >= 4096, k > 16 (b/572311831) stays.
Unchanged: CUDA still sorts the float key (#50426). NumPy-order and non-total compares are not encoded. Sorts that are not rewritten to rocprim stay on their existing path.

🎯 Justification
Enable more unit test on ROCm.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
🧪 Tests

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Admit 8-aligned kConcatenate in BlockLevelEmitterBackend.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Admit 8-aligned kConcatenate in BlockLevelEmitterBackend.

Lower the minimum non-final operand alignment in `IsTritonSupportedConcatenate`
from 64 to 8 elements and add `HloOpcode::kConcatenate` to
`BlockLevelEmitterBackend::IsSupported` so standalone concatenate fusions can be
autotuned with the Triton block-level emitter against the native emitter when
`xla_gpu_experimental_all_fusions_with_triton` is false.

Keep the 64-element alignment requirement on non-final concatenate operands in
both `GemmFusion` and `PriorityFusion` so neither pass fuses sub-64 concatenate
operands into GEMM or generic Triton fusions (where tiling search across
unaligned concatenate regions is expensive).

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Add HloComputation::HasCalledComputations() to skip leaf computation scans.

head_commit.message:
Add HloComputation::HasCalledComputations() to skip leaf computation scans.

Post-fusion XLA modules contain thousands of leaf fusion and reducer
computations that call no subcomputations, yet `CallGraph::Build`, `HloDCE`,
`MakeComputationPostOrder`, `RemoveUnusedComputations`,
`MakeEmbeddedComputationsList`, and `CollectivePipeliner` scan every
instruction in leaf computations looking for callees or `while` loops.

Expose `HloComputation::HasCalledComputations()` (backed by the existing
`callee_computations_` map) and combine it with
`HloInstruction::MightHaveCalledComputations()` on `instructions_with_info()`
to skip leaf computations in O(1) and skip non-calling opcodes without
chasing instruction pointers.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1005024627

PR #51244: [XLA] Fix Bazel 9 compatibility

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51244

This PR brings Bazel 9 compat to XLA, especially useful for downstream consumers like http://github.com/zml/zml otherwise stuck to bazel 8.

This PR doens't make Bazel 9 the default here (which would remove support for WORKSPACE), it only brings Bazel 9 compat while keeping Bazel 8 compat as well.

I'd favor merging this all at once, but let me know if you want me to split this into easier chunks.

The changes are fairly straightforward:
- Bump dependencies for Bazel 9 compatibility.
- Add explicit loads for external rules and providers.
- Update dependency patches and BUILD overlays.
- Declare missing module dependencies.

display_title: PR #48501: [ROCm] Add  `ProfileOptions.advanced_configuration` into the ROCm tracer (PR1)

head_commit.message:
PR #48501: [ROCm] Add  `ProfileOptions.advanced_configuration` into the ROCm tracer (PR1)

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/48501

First of three PRs that add `ProfileOptions.advanced_configuration` support to the ROCm tracer: this PR, #48502 (the parser) and #48503 (the wiring). This one is groundwork and adds no new options.

- Move `RocmTracerOptions` from `rocm_tracer.h` to `rocm_tracer_utils.h`, which has no ROCm dependency, so host-only targets (the parser in #48502) can use it. `rocm_tracer.h` already includes `rocm_tracer_utils.h`, so existing code is unaffected.
- Replace `AnnotationMap::Clear()` with `Reset(max_annotation_strings)`, which clears the entries and sets the capacity under one lock. The capacity was a `const` 1M. `RocmTracer::Enable()` calls `Reset()` before it starts the rocprofiler context.
- `AnnotationMap::Add()` checks the capacity once per event, so an event's annotation, ROCTX range and scope range ID are stored together or not at all. Before, the event that filled the last slot kept its annotation but lost its scope range ID.
- `RocmTracerOptions::max_annotation_strings` is a `std::optional` with no default. `Enable()` returns `InvalidArgument` if it is unset; 0 retains nothing.
- `RocmTraceCollectorOptions` fields default to 0 instead of being indeterminate, and its `max_annotation_strings`, which was set but never read, is removed.
- `hlo_op_profiler_rocm` drops its unused `//xla/service:gpu_plugin` dep, which `dwyu` flags once this PR edits the target's source, and depends on `rocm_tracer_utils` directly. `HloOpProfiler` takes an injected runner, and every binary that links it gets the plugin through `xla_test` or `matmul_perf_table_gen`, so link inputs don't change. `hlo_op_profiler_cuda` and `hlo_op_profiler_stub` still list it and can be cleaned up separately.

**Behaviour change:** `GpuTracer` sessions now get the 4M annotation capacity that `GetRocmTracerOptions()` already requested; `Enable()` ignored it and used 1M. The cap counts distinct strings, so most workloads won't see a difference (CUPTI's default is 1M). `hlo_op_profiler_rocm` keeps 1M. #48502 adds `gpu_max_annotation_strings` to set another value.

🎯 Justification

The ROCm `GpuTracer` ignores `advanced_configuration`: it reads only `device_type()`, so any `gpu_*` key a user sets, or misspells, is silently dropped. The CUPTI backend parses the map, but a bad key fails `Start()`, and `ProfilerController` then skips `CollectData()`, so the user loses the GPU trace with only a log line. #48502 and #48503 instead report problems in `XSpace.errors`/`warnings` and keep tracing. They need `RocmTracerOptions` in a header without ROCm dependencies, and an annotation capacity that can be set per session; this PR provides both.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

♻️ Cleanup, 🐛 Bug Fix

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Check operand tile sizes against the register limit before tiling

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Check operand tile sizes against the register limit before tiling

The register pre-check before `Tile()` looked only at root tiles and missed
e.g. the whole-row operand tiles of softmax-like reductions. Such candidates
were tiled and only then rejected by `DoesComputationFitInRegisters`.

Tile the fusion symbolically once per search, collect its register-resident
tiles (roots, fusion operands and iotas), and check each candidate by
evaluating their symbolic tile sizes.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 994380707

display_title: Plumb BlasLtMatmulAlgorithmProto into CublasLtMatmulThunk

head_commit.message:
Use proper algorithm descriptors for cuBLASLt

Previously `selected_algorithm` only stored an index into the heuristic result list returned by `cublasLtMatmulAlgoGetHeuristic`. Because that list depends on the device and cuBLASLt version, the same index can resolve to a different kernel across GPU SKUs or library updates.

Therefore this change captures the full cuBLASLt algorithm attributes in `BlasLtMatmulAlgorithmProto` and propagates them through autotuning, `GemmBackendConfig`, and `CublasLtMatmulThunkProto`. At runtime we reconstruct and validate the `cublasLtMatmulAlgo_t` descriptor from the proto and fall back to the heuristic index only when the descriptor is not supported (unless `xla_gpu_require_exact_blas_lt_algorithm` is enabled).

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1005398629

display_title: Ignore the optimized HLO module in XLA:GPU AOT golden verification

head_commit.message:
Ignore the optimized HLO module in XLA:GPU AOT golden verification

The optimized HLO embedded in GpuExecutableProto is documented as debug-only,
but nearly every compiler change rewrites it (shapes, instruction ids,
backend-config JSON, fingerprints), so golden verification keeps failing on
changes that leave the executable's runtime behavior intact. Thunks, program
shape, constant allocations and the module's runtime debug options are still
compared. Forward compatibility of emitted HLO and changed constant data are no
longer flagged by this check; loading old artifacts stays covered by the
BackwardsCompatibility suites.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1004675862

display_title: PR #47839: [XLA:GPU] Add cuDNN non-GEMM pointwise fusion support via TensorIR engine

head_commit.message:
PR #47839: [XLA:GPU] Add cuDNN non-GEMM pointwise fusion support via TensorIR engine

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/47839

## Summary

This PR adds support for lowering non-GEMM HLO pointwise fusions to the cuDNN graph API using the `CUDNN_GENERIC_MEMBOUND_FUSION_TENSOR_IR_ENGINE` (cuDNN's dedicated memory-bound TensorIR engine). The feature is controlled by a new flag `--xla_gpu_cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_level`.

### TensorIR engine selection

For non-GEMM (memory-bound) fusions, `PrepareGraph` in `cudnn_fusion_compiler.cc` sets `force_tensor_ir=true` in `EngineOptions`. In `CudnnGraph::Prepare` (`cuda_dnn.cc`), this deselects engines that report `NUMERICAL_NOTE_TENSOR_CORE` (the CUTLASS FALLBACK engines, eng0-eng2), leaving only `CUDNN_GENERIC_MEMBOUND_FUSION_TENSOR_IR_ENGINE` (eng3). GEMM fusions continue to use the full engine set.

### Extended `cudnn_fusion_compiler.cc`

- **Non-GEMM parameter setup**: Added a parameter-binding path for fusions with no gemm/conv adapter, using `DimensionsAndStrides` directly from the HLO shape.
- **Broadcast lowering**: Fixed same-rank and rank-expanding broadcasts. Non-trivial broadcasts are represented via a logical reshape + pointwise identity so cuDNN sees a full-shape virtual tensor.
- **Logical ops**: `kAnd`, `kOr`, `kNot` now map to cuDNN `LOGICAL_{AND,OR,NOT}` for `PRED`-typed operands (bitwise variants remain unsupported).
- **Clamp fix**: Corrected operand ordering to match XLA semantics: `min(max(value, lower), upper)`.
- **Constant handling**: Extended from scalar-only to any single-element constant (e.g. `s32[1]`, `f32[1,1]`). For non-GEMM/conv fusions, constants are always tagged `COMPILE_TIME_CONST`; GEMM/conv fusions keep the prior behavior of runtime scalar tensors for non-scalar-shaped inputs.
- **Compute type for compare**: `kCompare` derives its compute type from the first operand's type (inputs are the arithmetic type; output is `PRED`).
- **Reduce disabled for non-GEMM fusions**: `kReduce` (including rank-preserving reduction lowering) is now rejected with `UnimplementedError` when the fusion has no gemm/conv adapter; reduce support is unchanged for GEMM/conv fusions. Variadic (tuple-shaped) reduce remains unsupported everywhere.

### Autotuner integration

`IsSupportedCudnnFusion` in `xla/backends/gpu/autotuner/cudnn.cc` is extended to accept non-GEMM fusions that aren't already tagged with kCustom when `xla_gpu_cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_level >= 1`, enabling autotuning over cuDNN/Native emitter and other backends for these fusions.

### New flag

```
--xla_gpu_cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_level=<int>
  0: Disabled (default)
  1: Compile pointwise fusions with cuDNN
```

### Tests

`xla/backends/gpu/codegen/cudnn_test.cc` has broad coverage including: pointwise elementwise ops, broadcasts, logical ops, clamp, reciprocal (`f32`), concat, slice, reshape/bitcast, and various dtype combinations, with test names/traits reorganized and shapes reduced to keep runtime down. `cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_rewriter_test.cc` covers the rewriter pass itself, including the multi-concatenate skip case.

display_title: Require all consumed HloValue positions to allow buffer sharing

head_commit.message:
Require all consumed HloValue positions to allow buffer sharing

An `HloValue` can appear at multiple `HloPosition`s (for example via
`bitcast` or tuple views) that are consumed together by the same
instruction, such as a fusion reading both `x` and a reshaped view of
`x` through a `reverse`. Allowing output buffer sharing when only one
position permits in-place reuse, or checking only the defining
instruction, corrupts elements still read through the other view.

Require every `HloPosition` consumed by a user instruction to permit
sharing in `BufferAssigner::LiveRangeInterferes` and
`HeapSimulator::RunComputation`. In `HloDataflowAnalysis`, match
`(operand, operand_index)` directly against in-place input/output pairs
in `CanShareOperandBufferWithUser` so secondary views do not inherit
must-alias status, and check all `kLoop` fusion parameter uses in
`DoesNotUseOperandBuffer` before treating an operand buffer as unused.

display_title: [XLA:CPU] Deduplicate CPU sort instantiations via radix-sort key encoding and branchless integer sort.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Deduplicate CPU sort instantiations via radix-sort key encoding and branchless integer sort.

Apply radix-sort order-preserving unsigned-integer key encoding (`FloatFlip` for IEEE-754 floats and sign-bit flipping for two's-complement signed integers) to map 1D and 2D sort keys in-place into unsigned integers of matching byte width (`uint8_t`, `uint16_t`, `uint32_t`, `uint64_t`), sort them with `std::less<UIntKey>()`, and restore the original key bits afterward. This replaces 72 custom-comparator `std::sort` and `std::stable_sort` template instantiations (12 signed, unsigned, and floating-point key types × ascending/descending order across 1D and 2D key-value sorts) with 4 unsigned-integer sort instantiations, unlocking `libc++`'s branchless scalar integer sort (`cmp` + `cmov` sorting networks and explicitly instantiated `std::__sort` routines) while hoisting floating-point `NaN` checks, `half`/`bfloat16`-to-`float` promotions, and sort-direction branching out of the O(N log N) comparison loop into two branchless, auto-vectorized O(N) bitwise passes:

- Two's-complement signed and unsigned integers: flipping the sign bit shifts `[INT_MIN, INT_MAX]` monotonically onto `[0, UINT_MAX]`, and flipping all bits (`~0`, i.e. `MAX - u`) reverses unsigned `<` order for descending sorts. Because XOR is associative and self-inverse, `xor_mask = sign_bit_mask ^ dir_xor` combines both in a single bitwise XOR before and after sorting.
- IEEE-754 floating-point types (`half`, `bfloat16`, `float`, `double`): in sign-magnitude layout, positive floats (`sign == 0`) already increase with raw unsigned bits and only need the sign bit flipped (`u ^ kSignBit`), whereas negative floats (`sign == 1`) increase in magnitude in the opposite direction of `<` and need all bits flipped (`u ^ ~0`). Arithmetic right-shift `(signed(u) >> (W - 1)) | kSignBit` computes that mask branchlessly, falling back to comparator-based sorting only when a slice contains `NaN` or both `-0.0` and `+0.0`.

This shrinks `sort_lib.pic.o` by 1.01 MB (-41.5%) and speeds up 1D sorts by 3.45x-3.93x and 2D key-value sorts by 1.36x-1.84x with zero additional memory allocation (all key transforms operate in-place).

<details>

<summary>Expand for sort_thunk_test benchmark results</summary>

| Benchmark (`//xla/backends/cpu/runtime:sort_thunk_test`) | Baseline CPU (ns) | After CPU (ns) | Delta (%) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `BM_Sort1D<F32>/100000/1/0/1` | 9,534,839 | 2,765,621 | -71.0% |
| `BM_Sort1D<BF16>/100000/1/0/1` | 5,368,827 | 1,548,351 | -71.2% |
| `BM_Sort1D<F16>/100000/1/0/1` | 9,159,164 | 2,330,089 | -74.6% |
| `BM_SortKeyValue2D<BF16,S32>/1024/512/0/1` | 25,128,096 | 18,409,094 | -26.7% |
| `BM_SortKeyValue2D<BF16,S32>/64/4096/0/1` | 15,089,948 | 11,116,120 | -26.3% |
| `BM_SortKeyValue2D<F32,S32>/1024/512/0/1` | 31,951,047 | 17,405,757 | -45.5% |
| `BM_SortKeyValue2D<F32,S32>/64/4096/0/1` | 20,800,960 | 11,864,440 | -43.0% |

</details>

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Collapse contiguous minor dimensions on non-default layouts in Triton

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Collapse contiguous minor dimensions on non-default layouts in Triton

Hoisted boundary bitcasts on transpose fusions can produce non-default source or destination layouts where the two physically minormost dimensions are not the last two logical dimensions. Skipping minor-dimension collapsing in these cases prevents 128-bit vectorized global memory accesses and 4D TMA descriptor loads when the minormost dimension is narrower than 16 bytes.

Allow collapsing contiguous physical minor dimensions regardless of their
logical positions by tracking the merged dimension groups and emitting a reshape followed by a transpose (or the inverse before inserts) to restore the original logical axis order.

display_title: PR #48501: [ROCm] Add  `ProfileOptions.advanced_configuration` into the ROCm tracer (PR1)

head_commit.message:
PR #48501: [ROCm] Add  `ProfileOptions.advanced_configuration` into the ROCm tracer (PR1)

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/48501

First of three PRs that add `ProfileOptions.advanced_configuration` support to the ROCm tracer: this PR, #48502 (the parser) and #48503 (the wiring). This one is groundwork and adds no new options.

- Move `RocmTracerOptions` from `rocm_tracer.h` to `rocm_tracer_utils.h`, which has no ROCm dependency, so host-only targets (the parser in #48502) can use it. `rocm_tracer.h` already includes `rocm_tracer_utils.h`, so existing code is unaffected.
- Replace `AnnotationMap::Clear()` with `Reset(max_annotation_strings)`, which clears the entries and sets the capacity under one lock. The capacity was a `const` 1M. `RocmTracer::Enable()` calls `Reset()` before it starts the rocprofiler context.
- `AnnotationMap::Add()` checks the capacity once per event, so an event's annotation, ROCTX range and scope range ID are stored together or not at all. Before, the event that filled the last slot kept its annotation but lost its scope range ID.
- `RocmTracerOptions::max_annotation_strings` is a `std::optional` with no default. `Enable()` returns `InvalidArgument` if it is unset; 0 retains nothing.
- `RocmTraceCollectorOptions` fields default to 0 instead of being indeterminate, and its `max_annotation_strings`, which was set but never read, is removed.
- `hlo_op_profiler_rocm` drops its unused `//xla/service:gpu_plugin` dep, which `dwyu` flags once this PR edits the target's source, and depends on `rocm_tracer_utils` directly. `HloOpProfiler` takes an injected runner, and every binary that links it gets the plugin through `xla_test` or `matmul_perf_table_gen`, so link inputs don't change. `hlo_op_profiler_cuda` and `hlo_op_profiler_stub` still list it and can be cleaned up separately.

**Behaviour change:** `GpuTracer` sessions now get the 4M annotation capacity that `GetRocmTracerOptions()` already requested; `Enable()` ignored it and used 1M. The cap counts distinct strings, so most workloads won't see a difference (CUPTI's default is 1M). `hlo_op_profiler_rocm` keeps 1M. #48502 adds `gpu_max_annotation_strings` to set another value.

🎯 Justification

The ROCm `GpuTracer` ignores `advanced_configuration`: it reads only `device_type()`, so any `gpu_*` key a user sets, or misspells, is silently dropped. The CUPTI backend parses the map, but a bad key fails `Start()`, and `ProfilerController` then skips `CollectData()`, so the user loses the GPU trace with only a log line. #48502 and #48503 instead report problems in `XSpace.errors`/`warnings` and keep tracing. They need `RocmTracerOptions` in a header without ROCm dependencies, and an annotation capacity that can be set per session; this PR provides both.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

♻️ Cleanup, 🐛 Bug Fix

head_commit.message:
PR #51244: [XLA] Fix Bazel 9 compatibility

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51244

This PR brings Bazel 9 compat to XLA, especially useful for downstream consumers like http://github.com/zml/zml otherwise stuck to bazel 8.

This PR doens't make Bazel 9 the default here (which would remove support for WORKSPACE), it only brings Bazel 9 compat while keeping Bazel 8 compat as well.

I'd favor merging this all at once, but let me know if you want me to split this into easier chunks.

The changes are fairly straightforward:
- Bump dependencies for Bazel 9 compatibility.
- Add explicit loads for external rules and providers.
- Update dependency patches and BUILD overlays.
- Declare missing module dependencies.

display_title: Ignore the optimized HLO module in XLA:GPU AOT golden verification

head_commit.message:
Ignore the optimized HLO module in XLA:GPU AOT golden verification

The optimized HLO embedded in GpuExecutableProto is documented as debug-only,
but nearly every compiler change rewrites it (shapes, instruction ids,
backend-config JSON, fingerprints), so golden verification keeps failing on
changes that leave the executable's runtime behavior intact. Thunks, program
shape, constant allocations and the module's runtime debug options are still
compared. Forward compatibility of emitted HLO and changed constant data are no
longer flagged by this check; loading old artifacts stays covered by the
BackwardsCompatibility suites.

display_title: PR #48501: [ROCm] Add  `ProfileOptions.advanced_configuration` into the ROCm tracer (PR1)

head_commit.message:
PR #48501: [ROCm] Add  `ProfileOptions.advanced_configuration` into the ROCm tracer (PR1)

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/48501

First of three PRs that add `ProfileOptions.advanced_configuration` support to the ROCm tracer: this PR, #48502 (the parser) and #48503 (the wiring). This one is groundwork and adds no new options.

- Move `RocmTracerOptions` from `rocm_tracer.h` to `rocm_tracer_utils.h`, which has no ROCm dependency, so host-only targets (the parser in #48502) can use it. `rocm_tracer.h` already includes `rocm_tracer_utils.h`, so existing code is unaffected.
- Replace `AnnotationMap::Clear()` with `Reset(max_annotation_strings)`, which clears the entries and sets the capacity under one lock. The capacity was a `const` 1M. `RocmTracer::Enable()` calls `Reset()` before it starts the rocprofiler context.
- `AnnotationMap::Add()` checks the capacity once per event, so an event's annotation, ROCTX range and scope range ID are stored together or not at all. Before, the event that filled the last slot kept its annotation but lost its scope range ID.
- `RocmTracerOptions::max_annotation_strings` is a `std::optional` with no default. `Enable()` returns `InvalidArgument` if it is unset; 0 retains nothing.
- `RocmTraceCollectorOptions` fields default to 0 instead of being indeterminate, and its `max_annotation_strings`, which was set but never read, is removed.
- `hlo_op_profiler_rocm` drops its unused `//xla/service:gpu_plugin` dep, which `dwyu` flags once this PR edits the target's source, and depends on `rocm_tracer_utils` directly. `HloOpProfiler` takes an injected runner, and every binary that links it gets the plugin through `xla_test` or `matmul_perf_table_gen`, so link inputs don't change. `hlo_op_profiler_cuda` and `hlo_op_profiler_stub` still list it and can be cleaned up separately.

**Behaviour change:** `GpuTracer` sessions now get the 4M annotation capacity that `GetRocmTracerOptions()` already requested; `Enable()` ignored it and used 1M. The cap counts distinct strings, so most workloads won't see a difference (CUPTI's default is 1M). `hlo_op_profiler_rocm` keeps 1M. #48502 adds `gpu_max_annotation_strings` to set another value.

🎯 Justification

The ROCm `GpuTracer` ignores `advanced_configuration`: it reads only `device_type()`, so any `gpu_*` key a user sets, or misspells, is silently dropped. The CUPTI backend parses the map, but a bad key fails `Start()`, and `ProfilerController` then skips `CollectData()`, so the user loses the GPU trace with only a log line. #48502 and #48503 instead report problems in `XSpace.errors`/`warnings` and keep tracing. They need `RocmTracerOptions` in a header without ROCm dependencies, and an annotation capacity that can be set per session; this PR provides both.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

♻️ Cleanup, 🐛 Bug Fix

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Require all consumed HloValue positions to allow buffer sharing

head_commit.message:
Require all consumed HloValue positions to allow buffer sharing

An `HloValue` can appear at multiple `HloPosition`s (for example via
`bitcast` or tuple views) that are consumed together by the same
instruction, such as a fusion reading both `x` and a reshaped view of
`x` through a `reverse`. Allowing output buffer sharing when only one
position permits in-place reuse, or checking only the defining
instruction, corrupts elements still read through the other view.

Require every `HloPosition` consumed by a user instruction to permit
sharing in `BufferAssigner::LiveRangeInterferes` and
`HeapSimulator::RunComputation`. In `HloDataflowAnalysis`, match
`(operand, operand_index)` directly against in-place input/output pairs
in `CanShareOperandBufferWithUser` so secondary views do not inherit
must-alias status, and check all `kLoop` fusion parameter uses in
`DoesNotUseOperandBuffer` before treating an operand buffer as unused.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1005498933

display_title: PR #47839: [XLA:GPU] Add cuDNN non-GEMM pointwise fusion support via TensorIR engine

head_commit.message:
PR #47839: [XLA:GPU] Add cuDNN non-GEMM pointwise fusion support via TensorIR engine

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/47839

## Summary

This PR adds support for lowering non-GEMM HLO pointwise fusions to the cuDNN graph API using the `CUDNN_GENERIC_MEMBOUND_FUSION_TENSOR_IR_ENGINE` (cuDNN's dedicated memory-bound TensorIR engine). The feature is controlled by a new flag `--xla_gpu_cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_level`.

### TensorIR engine selection

For non-GEMM (memory-bound) fusions, `PrepareGraph` in `cudnn_fusion_compiler.cc` sets `force_tensor_ir=true` in `EngineOptions`. In `CudnnGraph::Prepare` (`cuda_dnn.cc`), this deselects engines that report `NUMERICAL_NOTE_TENSOR_CORE` (the CUTLASS FALLBACK engines, eng0-eng2), leaving only `CUDNN_GENERIC_MEMBOUND_FUSION_TENSOR_IR_ENGINE` (eng3). GEMM fusions continue to use the full engine set.

### Extended `cudnn_fusion_compiler.cc`

- **Non-GEMM parameter setup**: Added a parameter-binding path for fusions with no gemm/conv adapter, using `DimensionsAndStrides` directly from the HLO shape.
- **Broadcast lowering**: Fixed same-rank and rank-expanding broadcasts. Non-trivial broadcasts are represented via a logical reshape + pointwise identity so cuDNN sees a full-shape virtual tensor.
- **Logical ops**: `kAnd`, `kOr`, `kNot` now map to cuDNN `LOGICAL_{AND,OR,NOT}` for `PRED`-typed operands (bitwise variants remain unsupported).
- **Clamp fix**: Corrected operand ordering to match XLA semantics: `min(max(value, lower), upper)`.
- **Constant handling**: Extended from scalar-only to any single-element constant (e.g. `s32[1]`, `f32[1,1]`). For non-GEMM/conv fusions, constants are always tagged `COMPILE_TIME_CONST`; GEMM/conv fusions keep the prior behavior of runtime scalar tensors for non-scalar-shaped inputs.
- **Compute type for compare**: `kCompare` derives its compute type from the first operand's type (inputs are the arithmetic type; output is `PRED`).
- **Reduce disabled for non-GEMM fusions**: `kReduce` (including rank-preserving reduction lowering) is now rejected with `UnimplementedError` when the fusion has no gemm/conv adapter; reduce support is unchanged for GEMM/conv fusions. Variadic (tuple-shaped) reduce remains unsupported everywhere.

### Autotuner integration

`IsSupportedCudnnFusion` in `xla/backends/gpu/autotuner/cudnn.cc` is extended to accept non-GEMM fusions that aren't already tagged with kCustom when `xla_gpu_cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_level >= 1`, enabling autotuning over cuDNN/Native emitter and other backends for these fusions.

### New flag

```
--xla_gpu_cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_level=<int>
  0: Disabled (default)
  1: Compile pointwise fusions with cuDNN
```

### Tests

`xla/backends/gpu/codegen/cudnn_test.cc` has broad coverage including: pointwise elementwise ops, broadcasts, logical ops, clamp, reciprocal (`f32`), concat, slice, reshape/bitcast, and various dtype combinations, with test names/traits reorganized and shapes reduced to keep runtime down. `cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_rewriter_test.cc` covers the rewriter pass itself, including the multi-concatenate skip case.

display_title: [XLA:CPU] Deduplicate CPU sort instantiations via radix-sort key encoding and branchless integer sort.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Deduplicate CPU sort instantiations via radix-sort key encoding and branchless integer sort.

Apply radix-sort order-preserving unsigned-integer key encoding (`FloatFlip` for IEEE-754 floats and sign-bit flipping for two's-complement signed integers) to map 1D and 2D sort keys in-place into unsigned integers of matching byte width (`uint8_t`, `uint16_t`, `uint32_t`, `uint64_t`), sort them with `std::less<UIntKey>()`, and restore the original key bits afterward. This replaces 72 custom-comparator `std::sort` and `std::stable_sort` template instantiations (12 signed, unsigned, and floating-point key types × ascending/descending order across 1D and 2D key-value sorts) with 4 unsigned-integer sort instantiations, unlocking `libc++`'s branchless scalar integer sort (`cmp` + `cmov` sorting networks and explicitly instantiated `std::__sort` routines) while hoisting floating-point `NaN` checks, `half`/`bfloat16`-to-`float` promotions, and sort-direction branching out of the O(N log N) comparison loop into two branchless, auto-vectorized O(N) bitwise passes:

- Two's-complement signed and unsigned integers: flipping the sign bit shifts `[INT_MIN, INT_MAX]` monotonically onto `[0, UINT_MAX]`, and flipping all bits (`~0`, i.e. `MAX - u`) reverses unsigned `<` order for descending sorts. Because XOR is associative and self-inverse, `xor_mask = sign_bit_mask ^ dir_xor` combines both in a single bitwise XOR before and after sorting.
- IEEE-754 floating-point types (`half`, `bfloat16`, `float`, `double`): in sign-magnitude layout, positive floats (`sign == 0`) already increase with raw unsigned bits and only need the sign bit flipped (`u ^ kSignBit`), whereas negative floats (`sign == 1`) increase in magnitude in the opposite direction of `<` and need all bits flipped (`u ^ ~0`). Arithmetic right-shift `(signed(u) >> (W - 1)) | kSignBit` computes that mask branchlessly, falling back to comparator-based sorting only when a slice contains `NaN` or both `-0.0` and `+0.0`.

display_title: Plumb BlasLtMatmulAlgorithmProto into CublasLtMatmulThunk

head_commit.message:
Use proper algorithm descriptors for cuBLASLt

Previously `selected_algorithm` only stored an index into the heuristic result list returned by `cublasLtMatmulAlgoGetHeuristic`. Because that list depends on the device and cuBLASLt version, the same index can resolve to a different kernel across GPU SKUs or library updates.

Therefore this change captures the full cuBLASLt algorithm attributes in `BlasLtMatmulAlgorithmProto` and propagates them through autotuning, `GemmBackendConfig`, and `CublasLtMatmulThunkProto`. At runtime we reconstruct and validate the `cublasLtMatmulAlgo_t` descriptor from the proto and fall back to the heuristic index only when the descriptor is not supported (unless `xla_gpu_require_exact_blas_lt_algorithm` is enabled).

display_title: PR #51286: [XLA:GPU] Enable topk_special_floats_test on ROCm by encoding a plain float total-order key

head_commit.message:
PR #51286: [XLA:GPU] Enable topk_special_floats_test on ROCm by encoding a plain float total-order key

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51286

📝 Summary of Changes
`topk_special_floats_test` expects `+0` to rank above `-0`. On ROCm the large shapes are rewritten to rocprim, and rocprim's float radix sort treats `+0` and `-0` as equal, so the returned index is wrong. CUDA still uses the float key, and its existing skip stays.
**What we change:**
- `SortComputationAnalysis` records `is_total_order` (`compare->order() == ComparisonOrder::kTotal`).
- The key is encoded only when the device is ROCm, the key type has a negative zero, the comparator is a plain compare (`kDefaultOrder`, not the NumPy-order or weak-order pattern), and `order=TOTAL`. `OrderedIntegralFromFloat` bitcasts the key to a signed integer of the same width and XORs negative values with the signed maximum. This is the map `ComparisonExpander` uses. It is its own inverse, so `FloatFromOrderedIntegral` applies it again and bitcasts back to the float after the sort.
- F16 and BF16 keys become S16, F32 becomes S32, and F64 becomes S64. The keys-only kernel is `CubSortKeys` for `int16_t`, `int32_t`, or `int64_t`. Among float keys, pair sorts are rewritten only for F32, so an encoded pair key is S32, which the pair kernel already accepts.
- Which sorts are rewritten does not change. The deviceless scratch-size lookup is keyed by byte width, and that width is unchanged. The encode and decode add elementwise ops before and after the sort, only for ROCm total-order float sorts that are already rewritten to rocprim.
- The replacement is built in one place, as suggested in review. For non-NumPy sorts, custom-call element 0 is the sorted key (decoded when it was encoded) and element 1 is the values. `PairInOperandOrder` restores operand order when the key was operand 1. `UnpackResultPair` is removed. New instructions are created through the sort, so they keep its metadata.
- `FloatTotalOrder` checks the original keys-only case, `f32[1000]` descending: the rocprim key is S32 on ROCm and F32 on CUDA. `SortTotalOrder` covers f16, bf16, f32, and f64, both directions, on `[16,128]`, and compares the result with the interpreter. `FloatTotalOrderPairKeyAtOperand0` and `FloatTotalOrderPairKeyAtOperand1` check both operand orders with `AMDMI210DeviceInfo`. `FloatTotalOrderSpecialValues` executes +0, -0, both infinities, and both NaNs on ROCm and skips on CUDA.
- `topk_special_floats_test` is enabled on ROCm. The NVIDIA skip for batch == 1, n >= 4096, k > 16 (b/572311831) stays.
Unchanged: CUDA still sorts the float key (#50426). NumPy-order and non-total compares are not encoded. Sorts that are not rewritten to rocprim stay on their existing path.

🎯 Justification
Enable more unit test on ROCm.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
🧪 Tests

- Two's-complement signed and unsigned integers: flipping the sign bit shifts `[INT_MIN, INT_MAX]` monotonically onto `[0, UINT_MAX]`, and flipping all bits (`~0`, i.e. `MAX - u`) reverses unsigned `<` order for descending sorts. - IEEE-754 floating-point types (`half`, `bfloat16`, `float`, `double`): in sign-magnitude layout, positive floats (`sign == 0`) already increase with raw unsigned bits and only need the sign bit flipped (`u ^ kSignBit`), whereas negative floats (`sign == 1`) increase in magnitude in the opposite direction of `<` and need all bits flipped (`u ^ ~0`). display_title: Extract ResolveCudnnSupport and fail on uncompiled cuDNN ops

head_commit.message:
Extract ResolveCudnnSupport and fail on uncompiled cuDNN ops

Extract `ResolveCudnnSupport` into `xla/service/gpu/cudnn_support_utils.h` and lazily resolve `se::dnn::DnnSupport*` inside `CuDnnFusionCompiler` and `CuDnnCustomCallCompiler` only when a cuDNN fusion or custom call is actually encountered.

Before this change, compiling devicelessly without cuDNN deviceless compilation enabled would silently skip CuDnnFusionCompiler. Compilation succeeded, but the resulting executable failed at runtime when it tried to deserialize the cuDNN graph. With this change, we fail at compile time instead.

display_title: Plumb BlasLtMatmulAlgorithmProto into CublasLtMatmulThunk

head_commit.message:
Use proper algorithm descriptors for cuBLASLt

Previously `selected_algorithm` only stored an index into the heuristic result list returned by `cublasLtMatmulAlgoGetHeuristic`. Because that list depends on the device and cuBLASLt version, the same index can resolve to a different kernel across GPU SKUs or library updates.

Therefore this change captures the full cuBLASLt algorithm attributes in `BlasLtMatmulAlgorithmProto` and propagates them through autotuning, `GemmBackendConfig`, and `CublasLtMatmulThunkProto`. At runtime we reconstruct and validate the `cublasLtMatmulAlgo_t` descriptor from the proto and fall back to the heuristic index only when the descriptor is not supported (unless `xla_gpu_require_exact_blas_lt_algorithm` is enabled).

display_title: Enable bazel-diff on Windows and oneAPI and scope cquery to build targets

head_commit.message:
Enable bazel-diff on Windows and oneAPI and scope cquery to build targets

While most XLA GitHub Actions CI jobs in `xla/build_tools/ci/build.py` already use `bazel-diff` with `cquery` to filter presubmit runs to impacted targets, `XLA_WINDOWS_X86_CPU_GITHUB_ACTIONS` and `XLA_LINUX_X86_GPU_ONEAPI_GITHUB_ACTIONS` still run full builds on every PR. (`XLA_LINUX_X86_GPU_HERMETIC_ROCM_GITHUB_ACTIONS` is intentionally left without `bazel-diff` because the 2x `cquery` overhead exceeds the savings on that build-only job.)

So this change enables `use_bazel_diff=True` (`bazel_diff_use_cquery=True`) for Windows CPU and oneAPI, and tightens how `xla/build_tools/ci/bazel_diff.py` invokes `bazel-diff` across all jobs:

1. Passes `--build_tag_filters` and `--universe_scope` in `get_cquery_command_options`, constructs `--cqueryExpression` from `build.target_patterns`, and excludes `-//xla/stream_executor/sycl/...` on Windows so `bazel cquery` only analyzes each job's in-scope targets.
2. Passes `--excludeExternalTargets` (and `--bazelStartupOptions` to `get-impacted-targets`) so `bazel-diff` does not spawn a second Bazel server to run `bazel mod graph` or query `//external:all-targets`.
3. Writes only the already-filtered explicit targets to `filtered_impacted_targets.txt` without re-appending negative directory wildcards (`-//xla/backends/gpu/...`, `-//xla/service/gpu/...`, `-//xla/tpu/...`), avoiding loading excluded packages during `bazel build --target_pattern_file`.

Measured improvements on PR #51454 (CI scripts change) and PR #51508 (C++ CPU + GPU change) compared to baseline PR runs:

- `XLA Windows x86 CPU`:
  - Scopes `cquery` to the 6,752 Windows CPU targets (instead of failing on excluded SYCL/GPU packages across 34,676 targets) and builds only impacted targets (59 actions on PR #51454 and 4,742 actions on PR #51508, instead of 42,496 actions for a full 6,570-target build).
  - Cuts `bazel-diff get-impacted-targets` from **2m15s** to **2.1s** (by avoiding a second Bazel server) and `bazel build --target_pattern_file` on a 12-target change from **2m54s** to **14.3s** (reducing total `build.py` time from **10m56s** to **6m10s**).
- `XLA Linux X86 GPU ONEAPI`:
  - Scopes `cquery` to the 679 oneAPI targets (`100.6s` at base, `4.2s` at head) and skips the 34,652-action build when no oneAPI targets are impacted (**2m32s** in `bazel-diff` with `Decision=SKIP`).
- Existing Linux `bazel-diff` jobs (from scoping `cquery` via `--build_tag_filters` and `--universe_scope`):
  - Prevents GPU C++ changes from falsely marking ~1,020 GPU targets as `IMPACTED` on CPU jobs (on PR #51508, editing `dot_search_space.cc` impacted 3,474 targets on `XLA Linux x86 GPU T4`, 0 GPU targets on the CPU jobs, and only the 1 modified CPU test).
  - `XLA Linux x86 GPU T4`: `cquery` target count drops from **33,876** to **3,948** (**88% fewer targets**), cutting `bazel-diff` duration from **321s-329s** to **177.6s** (**45% faster**).
  - `XLA Linux x86 CPU`: `cquery` target count drops from **34,676** to **8,685** (**75% fewer targets**), cutting `bazel-diff` duration from **233s-253s** to **133.9s** (**45% faster**).
  - `XLA Linux ARM64 CPU`: `cquery` target count drops from **34,676** to **8,669** (**75% fewer targets**), cutting `bazel-diff` duration from **270s-463s** to **131.3s** (**51%+ faster**).
  - `XLA Linux x86 CPU WORKSPACE`: `cquery` target count drops from **34,582** to **8,683** (**75% fewer targets**), cutting `bazel-diff` duration from **274.5s** to **157.5s** (**43% faster**).

display_title: [XLA:CPU] Deduplicate CPU sort instantiations via radix-sort key encoding and branchless integer sort.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Deduplicate CPU sort instantiations via radix-sort key encoding and branchless integer sort.

Apply radix-sort order-preserving unsigned-integer key encoding (`FloatFlip` for IEEE-754 floats and sign-bit flipping for two's-complement signed integers) to map 1D and 2D sort keys in-place into unsigned integers of matching byte width (`uint8_t`, `uint16_t`, `uint32_t`, `uint64_t`), sort them with `std::less<UIntKey>()`, and restore the original key bits afterward. This replaces 72 custom-comparator `std::sort` and `std::stable_sort` template instantiations (12 signed, unsigned, and floating-point key types × ascending/descending order across 1D and 2D key-value sorts) with 4 unsigned-integer sort instantiations, unlocking `libc++`'s branchless scalar integer sort (`cmp` + `cmov` sorting networks and explicitly instantiated `std::__sort` routines) while hoisting floating-point `NaN` checks, `half`/`bfloat16`-to-`float` promotions, and sort-direction branching out of the O(N log N) comparison loop into two branchless, auto-vectorized O(N) bitwise passes:

- Two's-complement signed and unsigned integers: flipping the sign bit shifts `[INT_MIN, INT_MAX]` monotonically onto `[0, UINT_MAX]`, and flipping all bits (`~0`, i.e. `MAX - u`) reverses unsigned `<` order for descending sorts. Because XOR is associative and self-inverse, `xor_mask = sign_bit_mask ^ dir_xor` combines both in a single bitwise XOR before and after sorting.
- IEEE-754 floating-point types (`half`, `bfloat16`, `float`, `double`): in sign-magnitude layout, positive floats (`sign == 0`) already increase with raw unsigned bits and only need the sign bit flipped (`u ^ kSignBit`), whereas negative floats (`sign == 1`) increase in magnitude in the opposite direction of `<` and need all bits flipped (`u ^ ~0`). Arithmetic right-shift `(signed(u) >> (W - 1)) | kSignBit` computes that mask branchlessly, falling back to comparator-based sorting only when a slice contains `NaN` or both `-0.0` and `+0.0`.

This shrinks `sort_lib.pic.o` by 1.01 MB (-41.5%) and speeds up 1D sorts by 3.45x-3.93x and 2D key-value sorts by 1.36x-1.84x with zero additional memory allocation (all key transforms operate in-place).

<details>

<summary>Expand for sort_thunk_test benchmark results</summary>

| Benchmark (`//xla/backends/cpu/runtime:sort_thunk_test`) | Baseline CPU (ns) | After CPU (ns) | Delta (%) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `BM_Sort1D<F32>/100000/1/0/1` | 9,534,839 | 2,765,621 | -71.0% |
| `BM_Sort1D<BF16>/100000/1/0/1` | 5,368,827 | 1,548,351 | -71.2% |
| `BM_Sort1D<F16>/100000/1/0/1` | 9,159,164 | 2,330,089 | -74.6% |
| `BM_SortKeyValue2D<BF16,S32>/1024/512/0/1` | 25,128,096 | 18,409,094 | -26.7% |
| `BM_SortKeyValue2D<BF16,S32>/64/4096/0/1` | 15,089,948 | 11,116,120 | -26.3% |
| `BM_SortKeyValue2D<F32,S32>/1024/512/0/1` | 31,951,047 | 17,405,757 | -45.5% |
| `BM_SortKeyValue2D<F32,S32>/64/4096/0/1` | 20,800,960 | 11,864,440 | -43.0% |

</details>

name: CI ROCm
display_title: PR #51053: Fix NULL pointer dereference in HloEvaluator when evaluating a literal-less kConstant instruction

head_commit.message:
PR #51053: Fix NULL pointer dereference in HloEvaluator when evaluating a literal-less kConstant instruction

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51053

## Summary / Root Cause
`HloInstruction::CreateFromProto` (xla/hlo/ir/hlo_instruction.cc) constructs
a literal-less `HloConstantInstruction` whenever a `kConstant`
`HloInstructionProto` has no `literal` field set — regardless of the
`prohibit_empty_literal` parameter, which currently only governs an
*existing-but-empty* literal, not an *entirely absent* one. This state is
meant only for tooling that intentionally drops an oversized constant's
literal when dumping a module (`HloConstantInstruction::HasLiteral()` /
`DropLiteral()`).

If such a module is later evaluated, it crashes:
`HloEvaluator::GetEvaluatedLiteralFor()` unconditionally calls
`HloInstruction::literal()` whenever `IsConstant()` is true, which
dereferences the null `literal_` (`std::shared_ptr<Literal>`), producing a
SIGSEGV.

Found via a libFuzzer + ASan/UBSan harness targeting the
`HloModuleProto` deserialize → `HloEvaluator::Evaluate` path. Minimal
trigger: a single `kConstant` instruction proto with no `literal` field.

## The Fix

1. `HloInstruction::CreateFromProto`: when a `kConstant` proto has no
   `literal` and `prohibit_empty_literal` is true (the default used by
   every evaluation-facing caller — `run_hlo_module`, PJRT executable
   loading, etc.), return `absl::InvalidArgumentError` instead of silently
   constructing a literal-less instruction. Callers that genuinely need the
   "literal dropped" dump-only representation can still get it by passing
   `prohibit_empty_literal=false`.
2. `HloEvaluator::GetEvaluatedLiteralFor()` and
   `HloEvaluator::ExtractEvaluatedLiteralFor()`: added a `CHECK(HasLiteral())`
   defense-in-depth guard, consistent with the existing
   `CHECK(literal != nullptr)` a few lines below it, so that if any other
   path ever constructs a literal-less constant, evaluation fails with a
   clear diagnostic instead of a raw null-pointer SEGV.

## Impact

Prevents a denial-of-service crash (CWE-476, null pointer dereference) when
evaluating a malformed or maliciously crafted `HloModuleProto` whose
constant instruction is missing its literal payload. This affects any
consumer that deserializes and evaluates/interprets an `HloModuleProto` not
produced by XLA's own trusted compilation pipeline (the HLO interpreter
backend, `run_hlo_module`, or constant-folding over a less-trusted module).

## Behavior change to note for reviewers

Any existing caller that loads a "literal-dropped" dump **with**
`prohibit_empty_literal=true` and only inspects structure/shapes (never
evaluates) will now get an error instead of a literal-less instruction. That
matches the flag's documented intent ("prohibit empty literal") and we
believe no in-tree caller relies on the previous silent-success behavior for
this exact combination, but flagging it explicitly since it's the one
observable behavior change.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Lower compilation parallelism in ROCm CI to 4

head_commit.message:
Lower compilation parallelism in ROCm CI to 4

`build_tools/rocm/run_xla_ci_build.sh` and `build_tools/rocm/rocm_xla.bazelrc` set `--xla_gpu_force_compilation_parallelism=16` in `XLA_FLAGS`. On the shared AMD RBE workers (where 8 test containers run concurrently on the same host), spawning a 16-thread compilation thread pool per test process causes occasional `SIGKILL` (`(Killed)`) shard crashes during multi-threaded LLVM/LLD HSACO compilation.

So this change lowers `--xla_gpu_force_compilation_parallelism` to `4` in the ROCm CI configuration as part of an effort to eliminate flaky tests in the XLA AMD Instinct GPU CI.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add ScanRewriterTriton to the GPU compiler pipeline behind a flag.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add ScanRewriterTriton to the GPU compiler pipeline behind a flag.

Add the debug option `xla_gpu_experimental_enable_triton_scan` (default off). When it is set, `GpuCompiler` runs `ScanRewriterTriton` in `OptimizeHloPostLayoutAssignment` before `AssociativeScanRewriter`, so eligible associative `kScan` instructions become Triton scan fusions instead of reduce-window trees.

The rewriter only sets the fusion kind to `__triton`; the tiling is chosen later by `PriorityFusion`, `FusionBlockLevelRewriter` or the autotuner.

`GpuCompiler` only adds the rewriter on GPUs that Triton supports. A tiled scan computes one row per block, so scans with a dimension of at least 32768 also need at least 64 rows (`kMinRowsForLongScan`); otherwise the hierarchical scan of `AssociativeScanRewriter` is faster (crossover at 64 rows on H100 and 32 on B200). Shorter scans are faster with Triton at any batch size.

`CanTritonHandleScan` now rejects scans over any dimension other than the last one, for which the tiled Triton scan computes wrong results.

For a cumsum with an elementwise epilogue on f32[B, N], with B from 1 to 256 and N from 1024 to 262144, enabling the flag is never slower on H100 and B200. It is 1.05–2.9x (H100) and 1.06–2.8x (B200) faster for N < 32768, and up to 1.9x (H100) and 2.3x (B200) faster for N ≥ 32768 and B ≥ 64.

A top-p sampling mask (softmax, cumsum, compare and select) on f32[B, K] with B from 1 to 256 and K in {64, 128} compiles to a single Triton kernel: 1.3–1.5 µs instead of 3.3–4.5 µs on H100, and 2.5–3.1 µs instead of 5.9–8.4 µs on B200.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Group adjacent transpose dimensions for Triton block-level fusions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Group adjacent transpose dimensions for Triton block-level fusions.

Group adjacent contiguous dimensions into normalized 2D/3D shapes for loop and
input transpose fusions rewritten into Triton block-level fusions:

- Update `ShouldRewriteLoopTransposeFusion` to admit collapsible FP8 transposes
  where `rank < root->shape().dimensions().size()` and the collapsed minor
  dimension is divisible by 16 or a power of 2, while leaving BF16/F32
  collapsible transposes with the native emitter.
- Add `MaybeCollapseTransposeFusion` to replace collapsible transpose fusions
  with a collapsed transpose fusion flanked by zero-cost outer bitcasts before
  Triton block-level tiling and codegen, updating the HLO schedule when present.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Autotune num_warps variants for block-level fusions when top_k > 1.

`GetNumWarps` derives `num_warps` from the largest live tile size alone
(8 warps for tiles above 4096 elements). For some reduction and transpose
fusions, 2-4 warps are faster. When `xla_gpu_fusion_autotune_top_k_configs`
is greater than 1, also try `num_warps / 2` and `num_warps * 2` for each
candidate config (deduplicated). The default (`top_k = 1`) is unchanged.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Admit 8-aligned kConcatenate in BlockLevelEmitterBackend.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Admit 8-aligned kConcatenate in BlockLevelEmitterBackend.

Lower the minimum non-final operand alignment in `IsTritonSupportedConcatenate`
from 64 to 8 elements and add `HloOpcode::kConcatenate` to
`BlockLevelEmitterBackend::IsSupported` so standalone concatenate fusions can be
autotuned with the Triton block-level emitter against the native emitter when
`xla_gpu_experimental_all_fusions_with_triton` is false.

Keep the 64-element alignment requirement on non-final concatenate operands in
both `GemmFusion` and `PriorityFusion` so neither pass fuses sub-64 concatenate
operands into GEMM or generic Triton fusions (where tiling search across
unaligned concatenate regions is expensive).

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1003888903

display_title: Release donated buffers before setting definition_event concrete

head_commit.message:
Release donated buffers before setting definition_event concrete

In `PjRtStreamExecutorRawLoadedExecutable::Execute`, the cleanup closure holding `buffers_to_release` was attached via `definition_event.AndThen(...)`. Because `tsl::AsyncValue` runs waiters in LIFO order, a caller waiting on `GetReadyFuture().Await()` could wake up and destroy an external buffer before the `buffers_to_release` waiter finished dropping its `ScopedHold::kExternalReference`.

So this change passes the cleanup closure into `GetEventForComputeStreamSyncPoint` and `AllocateAndRecordEvent`, which runs the cleanup on the stream callback thread before marking `definition_event` concrete.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add ScanRewriterTriton to the GPU compiler pipeline behind a flag.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add ScanRewriterTriton to the GPU compiler pipeline behind a flag.

Add the debug option `xla_gpu_experimental_enable_triton_scan` (default off). When it is set, `GpuCompiler` runs `ScanRewriterTriton` in `OptimizeHloPostLayoutAssignment` before `AssociativeScanRewriter`, so eligible associative `kScan` instructions become Triton scan fusions instead of reduce-window trees.

The rewriter only sets the fusion kind to `__triton`; the tiling is chosen later by `PriorityFusion`, `FusionBlockLevelRewriter` or the autotuner.

`GpuCompiler` only adds the rewriter on GPUs that Triton supports. A tiled scan computes one row per block, so scans with a dimension of at least 32768 also need at least 64 rows (`kMinRowsForLongScan`); otherwise the hierarchical scan of `AssociativeScanRewriter` is faster (crossover at 64 rows on H100 and 32 on B200). Shorter scans are faster with Triton at any batch size.

`CanTritonHandleScan` now rejects scans over any dimension other than the last one, for which the tiled Triton scan computes wrong results.

For a cumsum with an elementwise epilogue on f32[B, N], with B from 1 to 256 and N from 1024 to 262144, enabling the flag is never slower on H100 and B200. It is 1.05–2.9x (H100) and 1.06–2.8x (B200) faster for N < 32768, and up to 1.9x (H100) and 2.3x (B200) faster for N ≥ 32768 and B ≥ 64.

A top-p sampling mask (softmax, cumsum, compare and select) on f32[B, K] with B from 1 to 256 and K in {64, 128} compiles to a single Triton kernel: 1.3–1.5 µs instead of 3.3–4.5 µs on H100, and 2.5–3.1 µs instead of 5.9–8.4 µs on B200.

display_title: Make SubgraphConverter::EmitInstruction iterative for all ops

head_commit.message:
Make SubgraphConverter::EmitInstruction iterative for all ops

`SubgraphConverter::EmitInstruction` previously only used an iterative worklist for elementwise ops, so deep chains of non-elementwise indexing ops (`bitcast`, `transpose`, `reshape`, `slice`) still recursed on the call stack and could overflow 512 KiB worker stacks.

Therefore this change precomputes operand indices when pushing an instruction onto the workstack and emits all in-subgraph operands iteratively before lowering the instruction itself.

display_title: Plumb BlasLtMatmulAlgorithmProto into CublasLtMatmulThunk

head_commit.message:
Use proper algorithm descriptors for cuBLASLt

Previously `selected_algorithm` only stored an index into the heuristic result list returned by `cublasLtMatmulAlgoGetHeuristic`. Because that list depends on the device and cuBLASLt version, the same index can resolve to a different kernel across GPU SKUs or library updates.

Therefore this change captures the full cuBLASLt algorithm attributes in `BlasLtMatmulAlgorithmProto` and propagates them through autotuning, `GemmBackendConfig`, and `CublasLtMatmulThunkProto`. At runtime we reconstruct and validate the `cublasLtMatmulAlgo_t` descriptor from the proto and fall back to the heuristic index only when the descriptor is not supported (unless `xla_gpu_require_exact_blas_lt_algorithm` is enabled).

display_title: Enable bazel-diff on Windows and oneAPI and scope cquery to build targets

head_commit.message:
Enable bazel-diff for Windows CPU and oneAPI XLA CI jobs

Most XLA GitHub Actions CI jobs in `xla/build_tools/ci/build.py` already use `bazel-diff` with `cquery` to filter presubmit builds to impacted targets, except for `XLA_WINDOWS_X86_CPU_GITHUB_ACTIONS` and `XLA_LINUX_X86_GPU_ONEAPI_GITHUB_ACTIONS`.

So this change enables `use_bazel_diff=True` (`bazel_diff_use_cquery=True`) for those two jobs as well. To make `bazel-diff` work cleanly and quickly on Windows and oneAPI, it also:

1. Passes `--build_tag_filters` and `--universe_scope` in `get_cquery_command_options`, constructs `--cqueryExpression` in `xla/build_tools/ci/bazel_diff.py` from `build.target_patterns`, and excludes `-//xla/stream_executor/sycl/...` on Windows so `bazel cquery` only analyzes in-scope targets.
2. Passes `--excludeExternalTargets` (and `--bazelStartupOptions` to `get-impacted-targets`) so `bazel-diff` does not spawn a second Bazel server to run `bazel mod graph` or query `//external:all-targets`.
3. Writes only the already-filtered explicit targets to `filtered_impacted_targets.txt` without re-appending negative directory wildcards (`-//xla/backends/gpu/...`, `-//xla/service/gpu/...`, `-//xla/tpu/...`), avoiding loading excluded packages during `bazel build --target_pattern_file`.

display_title: Initialize reserved field in ROCm grouped GEMM UserArguments

head_commit.message:
Initialize reserved field in ROCm grouped GEMM UserArguments

In `SetUserArgsKernelRaggedInNonContractingDim`, `SetUserArgsKernelRaggedInContractingDim`, and `SetUserArgsKernelRaggedInBatchDim`, `hipblaslt_ext::UserArguments` structs are constructed in dynamic shared memory (LDS) and copied to global memory. Because LDS is not zero-initialized at kernel launch and `arg.reserved` was never assigned, leftover LDS bytes could leak into `UserArguments::reserved` (which TensileLite uses internally for bias broadcast metadata) and corrupt vector bias addressing for individual groups.

So this change explicitly sets `arg.reserved = 0` in all three kernels and widens `bias_type` from `int8_t` to `int32_t` to match `UserArguments::biasType`.

head_commit.message:
Disable cuBLAS fallback in MxScaledDotExecutionTest

In `MxFp4Fp8MixedBatchedCorrectness`, the ROCm Triton backend does not support mixed FP4/FP8 scaled-dot inputs, so native MX hipBLASLt (`__cublas$lt$matmul$mx`) competes only against `HIPBLASLT_FISSION` (`__cublas$lt$matmul`). Because both backends allocate the same 64 MiB workspace and the test shape runs in a few microseconds, timing jitter occasionally causes `HIPBLASLT_FISSION` to win and fail the FileCheck assertion.

So this change sets `xla_gpu_cublas_fallback` to `false` in `MxScaledDotExecutionTest`, which marks `HIPBLASLT_FISSION` as an excluded fallback backend while keeping Triton and native MX hipBLASLt enabled.

head_commit.message:
Defer hipModuleUnload in RocmExecutor until executor destruction

Calling `hipModuleUnload` in `RocmExecutor::UnloadGpuBinary` when an executable is destroyed corrupts ROCm runtime state on MI350X (`gfx950`), causing subsequent `hipCUB` and `hipBLASLt` kernel launches in `//xla/backends/gpu/tests:sorting_test` and `//xla/tests:dot_operation_test` to fail intermittently with `HIP_ERROR_ContextIsDestroyed` or GPU memory access faults.

Therefore this change keeps loaded `hipModule_t` handles in `in_memory_modules_` until `~RocmExecutor()` while still removing the pointer-keyed entry from `gpu_binary_to_module_` when the reference count reaches zero. This way we avoid stale cache hits if a future HSACO buffer is allocated at the same heap address.

display_title: Make SubgraphConverter::EmitInstruction iterative for all ops

head_commit.message:
Make SubgraphConverter::EmitInstruction iterative for all ops

`SubgraphConverter::EmitInstruction` previously only used an iterative worklist for elementwise ops, so deep chains of non-elementwise indexing ops (`bitcast`, `transpose`, `reshape`, `slice`) still recursed on the call stack and could overflow 512 KiB worker stacks.

Therefore this change precomputes operand indices when pushing an instruction onto the workstack and emits all in-subgraph operands iteratively before lowering the instruction itself.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Answer MakeFreeChunksList from a merged occupied range index

GlobalDecreasingSizeBestFitHeap::MakeFreeChunksList visited every chunk overlapping a buffer's live window and sorted them by offset. That is O(N K log K) per heap of N buffers with K overlapping chunks. BufferIntervalTree now keeps a segment tree over the T schedule times whose nodes hold the merged occupied memory ranges. A query reads O(log T) of those lists in place of the tree walk over the K chunks; their pieces are sorted as before. The free lists, chunks and offsets are unchanged; trees that saw a Remove after their first query keep visiting their nodes.

display_title: [XLA] Memory-cost-aware latency hiding scheduler (kMemoryCost, aging, priced overlap)

head_commit.message:
[XLA] LHS: gate kMemoryCost on memory pressure near the peak

Far below a computation's memory peak, preferring releasers cannot lower
the high-water mark; it only reorders work and shifts the scheduler clock
that later tie-breaks (kAvoidWaste, kLessStall) measure against. On fp8
Qwen3 recipes that moved the weight-gradient reduce-scatter start and the
fp8 weight-gradient GEMMs feeding it to the other side of the attention
backward block, keeping their inputs live across the peak (+0.9 GB and
+1.6 GB), with none of the rule's decisions involving the moved ops.

kMemoryCost (and kMemoryHeld) now only decide while the tracker's live
memory is at least memory_aware_pressure_fraction (default 0.9) of the
computation's pre-scheduling peak, which the scheduler already computes
in ModulePressureState::InitializePressureStates. Exposed on GPU as
--xla_gpu_experimental_memory_aware_pressure_fraction; 0 disables the
gate. Existing MemoryCostSchedulerTest cases disable the gate, two new
cases cover it.

On the two Qwen3 recipes a fraction of 0.9 (and 0.95) restores the
baseline schedule exactly; 0.8 removes two thirds of the qwen3-8b
regression and all of qwen3-4b's; 0.7 removes none of it.
