head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add ScanRewriterTriton to the GPU compiler pipeline behind a flag.

Add the debug option `xla_gpu_experimental_enable_triton_scan` (default off). When it is set, `GpuCompiler` runs `ScanRewriterTriton` in `OptimizeHloPostLayoutAssignment` before `AssociativeScanRewriter`, so eligible associative `kScan` instructions become Triton scan fusions instead of reduce-window trees.

The rewriter only sets the fusion kind to `__triton`; the tiling is chosen later by `PriorityFusion`, `FusionBlockLevelRewriter` or the autotuner.

`GpuCompiler` only adds the rewriter on GPUs that Triton supports. A tiled scan computes one row per block, so scans with a dimension of at least 32768 also need at least 64 rows (`kMinRowsForLongScan`); otherwise the hierarchical scan of `AssociativeScanRewriter` is faster (crossover at 64 rows on H100 and 32 on B200). Shorter scans are faster with Triton at any batch size.

`CanTritonHandleScan` now rejects scans over any dimension other than the last one, for which the tiled Triton scan computes wrong results.

For a cumsum with an elementwise epilogue on f32[B, N], with B from 1 to 256 and N from 1024 to 262144, enabling the flag is never slower on H100 and B200. It is 1.05–2.9x (H100) and 1.06–2.8x (B200) faster for N < 32768, and up to 1.9x (H100) and 2.3x (B200) faster for N ≥ 32768 and B ≥ 64.

A top-p sampling mask (softmax, cumsum, compare and select) on f32[B, K] with B from 1 to 256 and K in {64, 128} compiles to a single Triton kernel: 1.3–1.5 µs instead of 3.3–4.5 µs on H100, and 2.5–3.1 µs instead of 5.9–8.4 µs on B200.

display_title: [XLA] Memory-cost-aware latency hiding scheduler (kMemoryCost, aging, priced overlap)

head_commit.message:
[XLA] LHS: gate kMemoryCost on memory pressure near the peak

Far below a computation's memory peak, preferring releasers cannot lower
the high-water mark; it only reorders work and shifts the scheduler clock
that later tie-breaks (kAvoidWaste, kLessStall) measure against. On fp8
Qwen3 recipes that moved the weight-gradient reduce-scatter start and the
fp8 weight-gradient GEMMs feeding it to the other side of the attention
backward block, keeping their inputs live across the peak (+0.9 GB and
+1.6 GB), with none of the rule's decisions involving the moved ops.

kMemoryCost (and kMemoryHeld) now only decide while the tracker's live
memory is at least memory_aware_pressure_fraction (default 0.8) of the
computation's pre-scheduling peak, which the scheduler already computes
in ModulePressureState::InitializePressureStates. Exposed on GPU as
--xla_gpu_experimental_memory_aware_pressure_fraction; 0 disables the
gate. Existing MemoryCostSchedulerTest cases disable the gate, two new
cases cover it.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Synchronize external reference count tracking in the PJRT C API.

head_commit.message:
Synchronize external reference count tracking in the PJRT C API.

Concurrent calls to `PJRT_Buffer_IncreaseExternalReferenceCount` and `PJRT_Buffer_DecreaseExternalReferenceCount` race on `PJRT_Buffer::external_references`, which is an unsynchronized `std::vector`. Under concurrent host transfers or multi-threaded buffer access, unsynchronized `push_back` and `pop_back` calls corrupt the vector and can cause premature reference count underflow or crashes.

Guard `PJRT_Buffer::external_references` with the existing `PJRT_Buffer::mu` mutex in `xla/pjrt/c/pjrt_c_api_wrapper_impl.h`.

Add multi-threaded unit tests in `xla/pjrt/c/pjrt_c_api_test.cc` and `xla/pjrt/c_api_client/pjrt_c_api_client_test.cc` that exercise concurrent external reference acquisition and release, and verify that the net reference count returns to zero.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Propagate `RandomAccessFile::Read` errors in `tsl::ReadBinaryProto` and `tsl::ReadTextProto`.

head_commit.message:
Propagate `RandomAccessFile::Read` errors in `tsl::ReadBinaryProto` and `tsl::ReadTextProto`.

Previously, `FileStream::Next()` in `xla/tsl/platform/env.cc` recorded `status_ = s` whenever `result.empty()` (including normal `absl::OutOfRangeError` at EOF), and `ReadBinaryProto` / `ReadTextProto` only checked `stream->status()` inside `if (!parsed)`. This caused three bugs:

1. **Lazy-open `NotFoundError` swallowed as empty proto (`OkStatus`)**: On filesystems where `NewRandomAccessFile` does not perform a synchronous stat RPC at open time (such as `tsl::GcsFileSystem::NewRandomAccessFile` on `gs://`), a missing object fails on the first `RandomAccessFile::Read()` call with `absl::NotFoundError` and `result.empty()`. `FileStream::Next()` stored `status_ = s` and returned `false` (0 bytes). Because an empty 0-byte stream is a valid wire-format and text-format protobuf message (all fields optional in proto3), `ParseFromCodedStream` and `TextFormat::Parse` succeeded (`parsed == true`), skipping `if (!parsed) { RETURN_IF_ERROR(stream->status()); }` and returning `absl::OkStatus()` with an empty default-initialized proto instead of `absl::NotFoundError`.
2. **Partial read followed by a non-EOF error ignored**: When `RandomAccessFile::Read()` returned partial bytes (`!result.empty()`) alongside a non-EOF error, `FileStream::Next()` ignored the error status and delivered the partial buffer; if a subsequent `Read()` failed after a valid wire-format prefix, `stream->status()` was ignored because `parsed` was `true`.
3. **Corrupt/truncated files returned `OutOfRange` instead of `DataLoss`**: On filesystems where `Read()` returns `absl::OutOfRangeError` at EOF, `FileStream::Next()` recorded `OutOfRange` into `status_` at EOF. When protobuf parsing subsequently failed on a corrupt or truncated file (`!parsed`), `RETURN_IF_ERROR(stream->status())` returned `OutOfRange` instead of `DataLossError("Can't parse ...")`.

Fix:
- In `FileStream::Next()` (`xla/tsl/platform/env.cc`), check `if (!s.ok() && !absl::IsOutOfRange(s))` before `if (result.empty())`, recording only non-EOF read errors in `status_` and returning `false` immediately. Normal EOF (`absl::IsOutOfRange(s)` with `result.empty()`) returns `false` while leaving `status_` as `absl::OkStatus()`.
- In `ReadBinaryProto()` and `ReadTextProto()`, check `RETURN_IF_ERROR(stream->status())` unconditionally before `if (!parsed)`.
- Add unit tests in `xla/tsl/platform/env_test.cc` covering empty/corrupt proto files, lazy-open `NotFoundError` propagation, and partial-read error propagation.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Deduplicate op-independent conversion helpers in `hlo_legalize_to_stablehlo`.

head_commit.message:
Deduplicate op-independent conversion helpers in `hlo_legalize_to_stablehlo`.

`HloToStablehloOpConverter<StablehloOpTy>` and `HloToStablehloCustomCallOpConverter<HloOpTy>` instantiate conversion patterns across all ~135 StableHLO and MHLO operations in `xla/mlir_hlo/mhlo/transforms/hlo_legalize_to_stablehlo/hlo_legalize_to_stablehlo.cc`. Previously, `convertAttributes`, `isDenseI64Array`, `convertDenseArray`, and `rewriteMhloOpAsCustomCall` were templated on `HloOpTy` / `StablehloOpTy` without `if constexpr`, causing `convertAttributes` and the region-inlining loop to be emitted separately for every op (and requiring an explicit 11-op `if constexpr` exclusion list in `convertAttributes` for MHLO-only ops without a `HloToStablehloOp` mapping). In addition, `hasPrivateFeaturesNotInStablehlo<HloOpTy>` checked the 10 XLA-private op types via runtime `isa<...>` in every pattern instantiation rather than compile-time `if constexpr`.

Make `isDenseI64Array`, `convertDenseArray`, `convertAttributes`, `convertTypesAndAttributes`, `convertRegions`, and `rewriteMhloOpAsCustomCall` non-template helpers operating on `Operation*`, check `hasPrivateFeaturesNotInStablehlo<HloOpTy>` at compile time with `if constexpr (llvm::is_one_of<HloOpTy, ...>::value)`, and guard `convertRegions` with `if constexpr (!HloOpTy::template hasTrait<OpTrait::ZeroRegions>())`. In addition, hoist `dyn_cast<mhlo::CustomCallOp>(hloOp)` out of the attribute loop in `convertAttributes`, mutate `NamedAttribute` values in place (`hloAttr.setValue(stablehloAttr)`), fetch `hloAttr.getName().getValue()` only after `dyn_cast<DenseIntElementsAttr>` succeeds in `convertDenseArray`, and pass `getPublicFeaturesNotInStablehlo(hloOp)` into `rewriteMhloOpAsCustomCall` instead of recomputing it.

Runtime and memory performance impact: Zero memory overhead (`+0.00%` allocations and peak memory) and `-2.23%` faster geomean CPU time (`-2.24%` wall time) across 8 `createHloLegalizeToStablehloPass` microbenchmarks.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Implement `Client::CancelExecution` in IFRT Proxy.

head_commit.message:
Implement `Client::CancelExecution` in IFRT Proxy.

`xla::ifrt::proxy::Client::CancelExecution` was previously a no-op stub, which prevented client-side execution cancellation (such as MPMD reshard cancellation) from propagating through IFRT Proxy to the server backend.

Bump the IFRT Proxy protocol version to `kCancelExecution` (26), add `cancellation_handle` to `LoadedExecutableExecuteRequest`, and introduce `CancelExecutionRequest` and `CancelExecutionResponse` in `ifrt_service.proto`. On the client, `LoadedExecutable::Execute` mints a `cancellation_handle` and returns a `ProxyCancellationHandle` wrapping it, and `Client::CancelExecution` sends `CancelExecutionRequest` to the server. On the server, `IfrtBackend` stores the underlying `CancellationHandle` from `LoadedExecutable::Execute` until the execution completes, is cancelled via `HandleCancelExecutionRequest`, or the executable is destroyed.

In-flight executions dispatched through `xla::ifrt::proxy::Client` can now be cancelled via `Client::CancelExecution`, with unit tests covering the client, executable, and backend handlers.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add ScanRewriterTriton to the GPU compiler pipeline behind a flag.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add ScanRewriterTriton to the GPU compiler pipeline behind a flag.

Add the debug option `xla_gpu_experimental_enable_triton_scan` (default off). When it is set, `GpuCompiler` runs `ScanRewriterTriton` in `OptimizeHloPostLayoutAssignment` before `AssociativeScanRewriter`, so eligible associative `kScan` instructions become Triton scan fusions instead of reduce-window trees.

The rewriter only sets the fusion kind to `__triton`; the tiling is chosen later by `PriorityFusion`, `FusionBlockLevelRewriter` or the autotuner.

`GpuCompiler` only adds the rewriter on GPUs that Triton supports. A tiled scan computes one row per block, so scans with a dimension of at least 32768 also need at least 64 rows (`kMinRowsForLongScan`); otherwise the hierarchical scan of `AssociativeScanRewriter` is faster (crossover at 64 rows on H100 and 32 on B200). Shorter scans are faster with Triton at any batch size.

`CanTritonHandleScan` now rejects scans over any dimension other than the last one, for which the tiled Triton scan computes wrong results.

For a cumsum with an elementwise epilogue on f32[B, N], with B from 1 to 256 and N from 1024 to 262144, enabling the flag is never slower on H100 and B200. It is 1.05–2.9x (H100) and 1.06–2.8x (B200) faster for N < 32768, and up to 1.9x (H100) and 2.3x (B200) faster for N ≥ 32768 and B ≥ 64.

A top-p sampling mask (softmax, cumsum, compare and select) on f32[B, K] with B from 1 to 256 and K in {64, 128} compiles to a single Triton kernel: 1.3–1.5 µs instead of 3.3–4.5 µs on H100, and 2.5–3.1 µs instead of 5.9–8.4 µs on B200.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Stop SpaceToBatchConverter unpropagatable-op walk at kReshape

head_commit.message:
Stop SpaceToBatchConverter unpropagatable-op walk at kReshape

## Description

In `SpaceToBatchConverter`, `SupportedOpForPropagation` does not support
`HloOpcode::kReshape`, so `PropagateOnUsers` always terminates `SpaceToBatch`
propagation at `kReshape` and inserts `BatchToSpace` before the reshape.
However, `DoesConvolutionFeedUnpropagatableOp` previously walked through
`kReshape` into downstream operations (such as token-space attention
custom-calls in Vision/Audio/Video Transformer patch-embedding stems and hybrid
CNN/Transformer backbones like SegFormer MiT), causing `ConvolutionVisitor::Run`
to skip `SpaceToBatch` on upstream convolutions whose propagation chain had
already terminated at `kReshape`.

Stop `DoesConvolutionFeedUnpropagatableOp` from recursing through
`HloOpcode::kReshape` so upstream convolutions before spatial-to-token reshapes
undergo `SpaceToBatch` conversion.

Also fix `last_overlap` in `ConvolutionVisitor::GetConvolutionDetails` when
`base_dilation_factor == inherent_low_padding` to `kernel_spatial_dim_size +
base_dilation_factor - 2` (instead of `kernel_spatial_dim_size`, which only
matched `base_dilation_factor == 2`) so each split produces `spatial_split_size
* base_dilation_factor` outputs.

Tests:
- //third_party/tensorflow/compiler/xla/service:space_to_batch_converter_test
PiperOrigin-RevId: 1005963862

display_title: Ignore element size and memory space in CommonPjRtClient::Delinearize.

head_commit.message:
Ignore element size and memory space in CommonPjRtClient::Delinearize.

XLA `Literal` shapes always clear `element_size_in_bits` to 0 (storing sub-byte elements unpacked at 1 byte per element) and use the default `memory_space`, whereas PJRT buffer shapes carry packed `element_size_in_bits` (for example, 4 for `S4`/`U4` or 2 for `S2`/`U2`) and the buffer's `memory_space` (such as `Layout::kHostMemorySpace`). Comparing `literal_layout != shape.layout()` in `CommonPjRtClient::Delinearize` therefore always evaluated `need_transpose = true` for every sub-byte buffer and every host-memory-space buffer, even when the rest of the layout already matched. For sub-byte transfers, that forced an unnecessary heap allocation and zero-fill of `staged_buffer` at the full unpacked byte size followed by an identity `TransposePlan::Execute` copy on top of `UnpackIntN`, leaving the direct `UnpackIntN` branch unreachable.

Compare layouts in `CommonPjRtClient::Delinearize` with `Layout::Equal().IgnoreElementSize().IgnoreMemorySpace()`, taking the direct unpack or `memcpy` fast path when layouts otherwise match (and guarding `std::memcpy` on 0-byte outputs). On `BM_DelinearizeInt4`, this speeds up `S4` delinearization by 3.1x–3.7x for cache-resident buffers (4 Ki and 1 Mi elements, reaching 31–37 GiB/s) and by 9.7x for 64 Mi-element buffers (48.1 ms to 4.95 ms) by avoiding transient 64 MiB `staged_buffer` page faults and copies.

Tested with unit tests in `//xla/pjrt:common_pjrt_client_test` covering matching default and non-default `minor_to_major` sub-byte layouts, odd-element tail-byte masking, transposed sub-byte layouts, `kHostMemorySpace` buffers (including 0-element spans), and end-to-end `BufferFromHostLiteral` to `ToLiteral` round-trips, alongside `BM_DelinearizeInt4` microbenchmarks.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add ScanRewriterTriton to the GPU compiler pipeline behind a flag.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add ScanRewriterTriton to the GPU compiler pipeline behind a flag.

Add the debug option `xla_gpu_experimental_enable_triton_scan` (default off). When it is set, `GpuCompiler` runs `ScanRewriterTriton` in `OptimizeHloPostLayoutAssignment` before `AssociativeScanRewriter`, so eligible associative `kScan` instructions become Triton scan fusions instead of reduce-window trees.

The rewriter only sets the fusion kind to `__triton`; the tiling is chosen later by `PriorityFusion`, `FusionBlockLevelRewriter` or the autotuner.

`GpuCompiler` only adds the rewriter on GPUs that Triton supports. A tiled scan computes one row per block, so scans with a dimension of at least 32768 also need at least 64 rows (`kMinRowsForLongScan`); otherwise the hierarchical scan of `AssociativeScanRewriter` is faster (crossover at 64 rows on H100 and 32 on B200). Shorter scans are faster with Triton at any batch size.

`CanTritonHandleScan` now rejects scans over any dimension other than the last one, for which the tiled Triton scan computes wrong results.

For a cumsum with an elementwise epilogue on f32[B, N], with B from 1 to 256 and N from 1024 to 262144, enabling the flag is never slower on H100 and B200. It is 1.05–2.9x (H100) and 1.06–2.8x (B200) faster for N < 32768, and up to 1.9x (H100) and 2.3x (B200) faster for N ≥ 32768 and B ≥ 64.

A top-p sampling mask (softmax, cumsum, compare and select) on f32[B, K] with B from 1 to 256 and K in {64, 128} compiles to a single Triton kernel: 1.3–1.5 µs instead of 3.3–4.5 µs on H100, and 2.5–3.1 µs instead of 5.9–8.4 µs on B200.

display_title: Decouple CUB radix sort scratch estimation from runtime FFI handlers.

head_commit.message:
Decouple CUB radix sort scratch estimation from runtime FFI handlers.

`xla.gpu.ext.cub_sort_keys` and `xla.gpu.ext.cub_sort_pairs` bundled compile-time scratch-size estimation (`CubSort{Keys,Pairs}Instantiate`) on the runtime execution FFI targets. During deviceless GPU cross-compilation and AOT serialization, `DevicelessEstimateCubSortScratchSize` resolves scratch sizes via `CubScratchSizeDevicelessLookup`, yet `CustomCallThunk` creation and `ThunkProto` serialization still invoked or rejected the non-serializable `int64_t` `ExecutionState` instantiate handler unused at runtime.

Follow `xla.gpu.ext.cub_scan_unassigned_scratch_size` across CUDA, ROCm, and SYCL: register `CubSort{Keys,Pairs}Instantiate` on `xla.gpu.ext.cub_sort_{keys,pairs}_unassigned_scratch_size` for `EstimateCubSortScratchSize`, and register `xla.gpu.ext.cub_sort_{keys,pairs}` with `instantiate = nullptr` so runtime custom-call thunks compile and serialize in deviceless AOT workflows.

display_title: [XLA] Treat block-scale dequantized weights as parameter-like in dot swapping

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Treat block-scale dequantized weights as parameter-like in dot swapping

- `AlgebraicSimplifierVisitor::MoveDotParamToRhs` swaps `dot(activations,
  weights)` when `enable_move_dot_param_to_rhs` is enabled and only the LHS
  looks parameter-like, which breaks RHS-only convolution input fusion when the
  weight goes through a block-scaled dequantization graph (`reshape ->

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add ScanRewriterTriton to the GPU compiler pipeline behind a flag.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add ScanRewriterTriton to the GPU compiler pipeline behind a flag.

Add the debug option `xla_gpu_experimental_enable_triton_scan` (default off). When it is set, `GpuCompiler` runs `ScanRewriterTriton` in `OptimizeHloPostLayoutAssignment` before `AssociativeScanRewriter`, so eligible associative `kScan` instructions become Triton scan fusions instead of reduce-window trees.

The rewriter only sets the fusion kind to `__triton`; the tiling is chosen later by `PriorityFusion`, `FusionBlockLevelRewriter` or the autotuner.

`GpuCompiler` only adds the rewriter on GPUs that Triton supports. A tiled scan computes one row per block, so scans with a dimension of at least 32768 also need at least 64 rows (`kMinRowsForLongScan`); otherwise the hierarchical scan of `AssociativeScanRewriter` is faster (crossover at 64 rows on H100 and 32 on B200). Shorter scans are faster with Triton at any batch size.

`CanTritonHandleScan` now rejects scans over any dimension other than the last one, for which the tiled Triton scan computes wrong results.

For a cumsum with an elementwise epilogue on f32[B, N], with B from 1 to 256 and N from 1024 to 262144, enabling the flag is never slower on H100 and B200. It is 1.05–2.9x (H100) and 1.06–2.8x (B200) faster for N < 32768, and up to 1.9x (H100) and 2.3x (B200) faster for N ≥ 32768 and B ≥ 64.

A top-p sampling mask (softmax, cumsum, compare and select) on f32[B, K] with B from 1 to 256 and K in {64, 128} compiles to a single Triton kernel: 1.3–1.5 µs instead of 3.3–4.5 µs on H100, and 2.5–3.1 µs instead of 5.9–8.4 µs on B200.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 982293610

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Accept C99 complex exp results for an infinite real part in complex_unary_op_test.

head_commit.message:
Accept C99 complex exp results for an infinite real part in complex_unary_op_test.

llvm/llvm-project#232791 changed MLIR's ComplexToStandard lowering of
complex.exp, which the XLA CPU and GPU backends use, to return the C99 Annex G
values when the real part is infinite and the imaginary part is not finite:
exp(-inf + I*y) = 0 + 0*I and exp(+inf + I*y) = inf + NaN*I. Before, it
returned NaN + NaN*I, which is what complex_unary_op_samples.h expects.

ExpTest now skips those samples, and a new ExpInfRealNonFiniteImag test checks
these inputs (including y = NaN) and accepts either the old NaN + NaN*I result
or the C99 value. The test then passes with both old and new LLVM.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1005838599

display_title: Stop SpaceToBatchConverter unpropagatable-op walk at kReshape

head_commit.message:
Stop SpaceToBatchConverter unpropagatable-op walk at kReshape

## Description

In `SpaceToBatchConverter`, `SupportedOpForPropagation` does not support
`HloOpcode::kReshape`, so `PropagateOnUsers` always terminates `SpaceToBatch`
propagation at `kReshape` and inserts `BatchToSpace` before the reshape.
However, `DoesConvolutionFeedUnpropagatableOp` previously walked through
`kReshape` into downstream operations (such as token-space attention
custom-calls in Vision/Audio/Video Transformer patch-embedding stems and hybrid
CNN/Transformer backbones like SegFormer MiT), causing `ConvolutionVisitor::Run`
to skip `SpaceToBatch` on upstream convolutions whose propagation chain had
already terminated at `kReshape`.

Stop `DoesConvolutionFeedUnpropagatableOp` from recursing through
`HloOpcode::kReshape` so upstream convolutions before spatial-to-token reshapes
undergo `SpaceToBatch` conversion.

Tests:
- //third_party/tensorflow/compiler/xla/service:space_to_batch_converter_test
PiperOrigin-RevId: 1000818479

head_commit.message:
Accept C99 complex exp results for an infinite real part in complex_unary_op_test.

llvm/llvm-project#232791 changed MLIR's ComplexToStandard lowering of
complex.exp, which the XLA CPU and GPU backends use, to return the C99 Annex G
values when the real part is infinite and the imaginary part is not finite:
exp(-inf + I*y) = 0 + 0*I and exp(+inf + I*y) = inf + NaN*I. Before, it
returned NaN + NaN*I, which is what complex_unary_op_samples.h expects.

ExpTest now skips those samples, and a new ExpInfRealNonFiniteImag test checks
these inputs (including y = NaN) and accepts either the old NaN + NaN*I result
or the C99 value. The test then passes with both old and new LLVM.

display_title: Implement `Client::CancelExecution` in IFRT Proxy.

head_commit.message:
Implement `Client::CancelExecution` in IFRT Proxy.

`xla::ifrt::proxy::Client::CancelExecution` was previously a no-op stub, which prevented client-side execution cancellation (such as MPMD reshard cancellation) from propagating through IFRT Proxy to the server backend.

Bump the IFRT Proxy protocol version to `kCancelExecution` (26), add `cancellation_handle` to `LoadedExecutableExecuteRequest`, and introduce `CancelExecutionRequest` and `CancelExecutionResponse` in `ifrt_service.proto`. On the client, `LoadedExecutable::Execute` mints a `cancellation_handle` and returns a `ProxyCancellationHandle` wrapping it, and `Client::CancelExecution` sends `CancelExecutionRequest` to the server. On the server, `IfrtBackend` stores the underlying `CancellationHandle` from `LoadedExecutable::Execute` until the execution completes, is cancelled via `HandleCancelExecutionRequest`, or the executable is destroyed.

In-flight executions dispatched through `xla::ifrt::proxy::Client` can now be cancelled via `Client::CancelExecution`, with unit tests covering the client, executable, and backend handlers.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Synchronize external reference count tracking in the PJRT C API.

head_commit.message:
Synchronize external reference count tracking in the PJRT C API.

Concurrent calls to `PJRT_Buffer_IncreaseExternalReferenceCount` and `PJRT_Buffer_DecreaseExternalReferenceCount` race on `PJRT_Buffer::external_references`, which is an unsynchronized `std::vector`. Under concurrent host transfers or multi-threaded buffer access, unsynchronized `push_back` and `pop_back` calls corrupt the vector and can cause premature reference count underflow or crashes.

Guard `PJRT_Buffer::external_references` with the existing `PJRT_Buffer::mu` mutex in `xla/pjrt/c/pjrt_c_api_wrapper_impl.h`.

Add multi-threaded unit tests in `xla/pjrt/c/pjrt_c_api_test.cc` and `xla/pjrt/c_api_client/pjrt_c_api_client_test.cc` that exercise concurrent external reference acquisition and release, and verify that the net reference count returns to zero.

display_title: PR #51053: Fix NULL pointer dereference in HloEvaluator when evaluating a literal-less kConstant instruction

head_commit.message:
PR #51053: Fix NULL pointer dereference in HloEvaluator when evaluating a literal-less kConstant instruction

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51053

## Summary / Root Cause
`HloInstruction::CreateFromProto` (xla/hlo/ir/hlo_instruction.cc) constructs
a literal-less `HloConstantInstruction` whenever a `kConstant`
`HloInstructionProto` has no `literal` field set — regardless of the
`prohibit_empty_literal` parameter, which currently only governs an
*existing-but-empty* literal, not an *entirely absent* one. This state is
meant only for tooling that intentionally drops an oversized constant's
literal when dumping a module (`HloConstantInstruction::HasLiteral()` /
`DropLiteral()`).

If such a module is later evaluated, it crashes:
`HloEvaluator::GetEvaluatedLiteralFor()` unconditionally calls
`HloInstruction::literal()` whenever `IsConstant()` is true, which
dereferences the null `literal_` (`std::shared_ptr<Literal>`), producing a
SIGSEGV.

Found via a libFuzzer + ASan/UBSan harness targeting the
`HloModuleProto` deserialize → `HloEvaluator::Evaluate` path. Minimal
trigger: a single `kConstant` instruction proto with no `literal` field.

## The Fix

1. `HloInstruction::CreateFromProto`: when a `kConstant` proto has no
   `literal` and `prohibit_empty_literal` is true (the default used by
   every evaluation-facing caller — `run_hlo_module`, PJRT executable
   loading, etc.), return `absl::InvalidArgumentError` instead of silently
   constructing a literal-less instruction. Callers that genuinely need the
   "literal dropped" dump-only representation can still get it by passing
   `prohibit_empty_literal=false`.
2. `HloEvaluator::GetEvaluatedLiteralFor()` and
   `HloEvaluator::ExtractEvaluatedLiteralFor()`: added a `CHECK(HasLiteral())`
   defense-in-depth guard, consistent with the existing
   `CHECK(literal != nullptr)` a few lines below it, so that if any other
   path ever constructs a literal-less constant, evaluation fails with a
   clear diagnostic instead of a raw null-pointer SEGV.

## Impact

Prevents a denial-of-service crash (CWE-476, null pointer dereference) when
evaluating a malformed or maliciously crafted `HloModuleProto` whose
constant instruction is missing its literal payload. This affects any
consumer that deserializes and evaluates/interprets an `HloModuleProto` not
produced by XLA's own trusted compilation pipeline (the HLO interpreter
backend, `run_hlo_module`, or constant-folding over a less-trusted module).

## Behavior change to note for reviewers

Any existing caller that loads a "literal-dropped" dump **with**
`prohibit_empty_literal=true` and only inspects structure/shapes (never
evaluates) will now get an error instead of a literal-less instruction. That
matches the flag's documented intent ("prohibit empty literal") and we
believe no in-tree caller relies on the previous silent-success behavior for
this exact combination, but flagging it explicitly since it's the one
observable behavior change.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Add DeserializeLoadedExecutable RPC to IFRT Proxy

head_commit.message:
Add DeserializeLoadedExecutable RPC to IFRT Proxy

Adds protocol version 26 and a new IfrtRequest/IfrtResponse pair so a client
can load a serialized executable on the server backend.

Client: Compiler::DeserializeLoadedExecutable uploads the bytes through the
host buffer store, sends the request, and builds the executable from the
CompileResponse. It returns Unimplemented if the server is older than
version 26, and rejects host callbacks.

Server: IfrtBackend handles the request on the compile thread pool, waits for
the uploaded bytes, calls the default Compiler, and returns the same
CompileResponse as Compile. The Compile response code is now shared.

The previous Unimplemented error cited an unstable serialization format. That is
not a concern here: the proxy never reads the bytes and sends them unchanged.
The server backend that loads them checks that they match its own runtime and
returns an error status if they do not. The same compatibility rule applies to
any IFRT client that loads a serialized executable.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1000592516

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Check all consumed operand positions before sharing buffers

head_commit.message:
Check all consumed operand positions before sharing buffers

When an `HloValue` has multiple positions (for example, `x` and `bitcast(x)`), all positions share the same underlying buffer. Previously, `BufferAssigner::LiveRangeInterferes` allowed buffer sharing if any consumed position passed `CanShareOperandBufferWithUser`, and `HeapSimulator::RunComputation` only checked the defining position.

Therefore this change requires every position of the operand value consumed by the user instruction to allow buffer sharing in both `BufferAssigner` and `HeapSimulator`. This prevents in-place instructions from overwriting an input buffer before reading it through a bitcast.

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/51490

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1005776439

display_title: Support BlasLtMatmulAlgorithm in CUDA BlasLt

head_commit.message:
Support BlasLtMatmulAlgorithmProto in CUDA BlasLt

Heuristic indices returned by `cublasLtMatmulAlgoGetHeuristic` depend on the GPU and cuBLASLt version, so the same index can resolve to a different kernel across devices or library updates.

Therefore this change introduces `BlasLtMatmulAlgorithmProto` in `xla/stream_executor/gpu/gpu_blas_lt.proto` to capture the full cuBLASLt algorithm configuration and numerical implementation flags. `cuda::BlasLt::MatmulPlan` now populates this proto when querying heuristic algorithms, and `MatmulPlan::SetCachedAlgorithm` reconstructs and validates the exact `cublasLtMatmulAlgo_t` descriptor from the proto (falling back to the heuristic index when needed unless `require_exact_algorithm` is set).

display_title: Add support for C32 and BC32 core types

head_commit.message:
Add support for C32 and BC32 core types

Add C32 (complex<f16>) and BC32 (complex<bf16>) to XLA core HLO and
Literals with four-byte, non-arithmetic XLA-owned storage carriers.
Define PrimitiveType values and LiteralProto byte fields with
interleaved little-endian components. Support HLO text and Literal
round-trips.

Support literal movement and real/imag/complex/convert in the
evaluator, and dispatch complex abs on the operand type. Reject
other operations on the new types and remaining C32/BC32 before
CPU/GPU code generation, covering JIT and AOT compilation.

Support the carriers in compare-literals, skip unsupported constant
inversion in algebraic simplification, and reject unsupported uses
in reduction collectives, literal translation and the driver.

Refs openxla/xla#6136.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Decouple CUB radix sort scratch estimation from runtime FFI handlers.

head_commit.message:
Decouple CUB radix sort scratch estimation from runtime FFI handlers.

`xla.gpu.ext.cub_sort_keys` and `xla.gpu.ext.cub_sort_pairs` bundled compile-time scratch-size estimation (`CubSort{Keys,Pairs}Instantiate`) on the runtime execution FFI targets. During deviceless GPU cross-compilation and AOT serialization, `DevicelessEstimateCubSortScratchSize` resolves scratch sizes via `CubScratchSizeDevicelessLookup`, yet `CustomCallThunk` creation and `ThunkProto` serialization still invoked or rejected the non-serializable `int64_t` `ExecutionState` instantiate handler unused at runtime.

Follow `xla.gpu.ext.cub_scan_unassigned_scratch_size` across CUDA, ROCm, and SYCL: register `CubSort{Keys,Pairs}Instantiate` on `xla.gpu.ext.cub_sort_{keys,pairs}_unassigned_scratch_size` for `EstimateCubSortScratchSize`, and register `xla.gpu.ext.cub_sort_{keys,pairs}` with `instantiate = nullptr` so runtime custom-call thunks compile and serialize in deviceless AOT workflows.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1005252784

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add ScanRewriterTriton to the GPU compiler pipeline behind a flag.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add ScanRewriterTriton to the GPU compiler pipeline behind a flag.

Add the debug option `xla_gpu_experimental_enable_triton_scan` (default off). When it is set, `GpuCompiler` runs `ScanRewriterTriton` in `OptimizeHloPostLayoutAssignment` before `AssociativeScanRewriter`, so eligible associative `kScan` instructions become Triton scan fusions instead of reduce-window trees.

The rewriter only sets the fusion kind to `__triton`; the tiling is chosen later by `PriorityFusion`, `FusionBlockLevelRewriter` or the autotuner.

`GpuCompiler` only adds the rewriter on GPUs that Triton supports. A tiled scan computes one row per block, so scans with a dimension of at least 32768 also need at least 64 rows (`kMinRowsForLongScan`); otherwise the hierarchical scan of `AssociativeScanRewriter` is faster (crossover at 64 rows on H100 and 32 on B200). Shorter scans are faster with Triton at any batch size.

`CanTritonHandleScan` now rejects scans over any dimension other than the last one, for which the tiled Triton scan computes wrong results.

For a cumsum with an elementwise epilogue on f32[B, N], with B from 1 to 256 and N from 1024 to 262144, enabling the flag is never slower on H100 and B200. It is 1.05–2.9x (H100) and 1.06–2.8x (B200) faster for N < 32768, and up to 1.9x (H100) and 2.3x (B200) faster for N ≥ 32768 and B ≥ 64.

A top-p sampling mask (softmax, cumsum, compare and select) on f32[B, K] with B from 1 to 256 and K in {64, 128} compiles to a single Triton kernel: 1.3–1.5 µs instead of 3.3–4.5 µs on H100, and 2.5–3.1 µs instead of 5.9–8.4 µs on B200.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 982293610

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Synchronize external reference count tracking in the PJRT C API.

head_commit.message:
Synchronize external reference count tracking in the PJRT C API.

Concurrent calls to `PJRT_Buffer_IncreaseExternalReferenceCount` and `PJRT_Buffer_DecreaseExternalReferenceCount` race on `PJRT_Buffer::external_references`, which is an unsynchronized `std::vector`. Under concurrent host transfers or multi-threaded buffer access, unsynchronized `push_back` and `pop_back` calls corrupt the vector and can cause premature reference count underflow or crashes.

Guard `PJRT_Buffer::external_references` with the existing `PJRT_Buffer::mu` mutex in `xla/pjrt/c/pjrt_c_api_wrapper_impl.h`.

Add multi-threaded unit tests in `xla/pjrt/c/pjrt_c_api_test.cc` and `xla/pjrt/c_api_client/pjrt_c_api_client_test.cc` that exercise concurrent external reference acquisition and release, and verify that the net reference count returns to zero.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1001719588

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Convert <=8-bit integer and F32 dot operands to BF16 by default.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Convert <=8-bit integer and F32 dot operands to BF16 by default.

Every <=8-bit integer value (`S4`, `U4`, `S8`, `U8`) is losslessly representable in `BF16` (which has 8 significand bits). Previously, `DotOperandConverter` upcasted the integer operand of a mixed `(int<=8, f32)` `dot` to `F32`, forcing the `dot` onto the TF32 Tensor Core path (`dot(f32, f32) -> f32`) even when `PrecisionConfig` had default precision (`ALG_UNSET` and `DEFAULT` operand precision).

Update `DotOperandConverter` so that when a `dot` with `F32` or `BF16` output and default precision multiplies an <=8-bit integer operand by an `F32` operand, both operands are converted to `BF16` (`dot(bf16, bf16) -> f32`/`bf16`). Explicit higher precision requests (`HIGH`, `HIGHEST`, or explicit `DotAlgorithm`s) continue to upcast to `F32`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1004256933

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Propagate tile constraints in XTile indexing emission to elide bounds masks.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Propagate tile constraints in XTile indexing emission to elide bounds masks.

When tiling `concatenate` regions in XTile, `SymbolicTileAnalysis` records branch-specific range constraints on each operand `Tile` (such as `offset in [0, N)` inside its active `scf.if` branch), but `EvaluateTilingParameters` previously ignored `TiledHloInstruction::tile().constraints()` when constructing the `IndexingMap` for `xla.apply_indexing`. As a result, `IsGuaranteedInBounds` evaluated the unconstrained `IndexingMap` domain across all `concatenate` branches—which can include negative offsets or offsets exceeding an individual operand's dimension—forcing unnecessary per-element bounds masks (`arith.cmpi` + `arith.andi`) on tile-aligned `concatenate` operand loads.

Attach an `xla.range` attribute to `xla.apply_indexing` operations in `EvaluateTilingParameters` whenever simplifying the `IndexingMap` with the tile's constraints tightens the result interval, preserve scaled `xla.range` attributes in `TritonXlaCollapseContiguousMinorDimsPass`, and use `xla::GetRange` in `IsGuaranteedInBounds` and `TritonXlaCollapseContiguousMinorDimsPass` so `xla.range` constraints are respected during Triton pointer and mask lowering.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1004246686

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Stop SpaceToBatchConverter unpropagatable-op walk at kReshape

head_commit.message:
Stop SpaceToBatchConverter unpropagatable-op walk at kReshape

## Description

In `SpaceToBatchConverter`, `SupportedOpForPropagation` does not support
`HloOpcode::kReshape`, so `PropagateOnUsers` always terminates `SpaceToBatch`
propagation at `kReshape` and inserts `BatchToSpace` before the reshape.
However, `DoesConvolutionFeedUnpropagatableOp` previously walked through
`kReshape` into downstream operations (such as token-space attention
custom-calls in Vision/Audio/Video Transformer patch-embedding stems and hybrid
CNN/Transformer backbones like SegFormer MiT), causing `ConvolutionVisitor::Run`
to skip `SpaceToBatch` on upstream convolutions whose propagation chain had
already terminated at `kReshape`.

Stop `DoesConvolutionFeedUnpropagatableOp` from recursing through
`HloOpcode::kReshape` so upstream convolutions before spatial-to-token reshapes
undergo `SpaceToBatch` conversion.

Tests:
- //third_party/tensorflow/compiler/xla/service:space_to_batch_converter_test
PiperOrigin-RevId: 1000818479

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Speed up single-threaded `GetMatchingPaths` and `FileSystem::IsDirectory`.

head_commit.message:
Speed up single-threaded `GetMatchingPaths` and `FileSystem::IsDirectory`.

In `GetMatchingPaths`, each `parent` directory in the queue has already been matched at previous levels, so we only need to match each `child` entry against the current segment's basename (`base_pattern`) rather than joining `parent` and `child` and re-matching the full path prefix. This avoids both re-evaluating earlier path components in `Match` and allocating joined path strings for non-matching entries.

Additionally, skip `GetChildren` when `base_pattern` contains no glob characters, avoid redundant `FileExists` calls on entries returned by `GetChildren`, reuse the `children` vector across iterations, and remove the redundant `FileExists` check before `Stat` in `FileSystem::IsDirectory`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1005739160

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add ScanRewriterTriton to the GPU compiler pipeline behind a flag.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add ScanRewriterTriton to the GPU compiler pipeline behind a flag.

Add the debug option `xla_gpu_experimental_enable_triton_scan` (default off). When it is set, `GpuCompiler` runs `ScanRewriterTriton` in `OptimizeHloPostLayoutAssignment` before `AssociativeScanRewriter`, so eligible associative `kScan` instructions become Triton scan fusions instead of reduce-window trees.

The rewriter only sets the fusion kind to `__triton`; the tiling is chosen later by `PriorityFusion`, `FusionBlockLevelRewriter` or the autotuner.

`GpuCompiler` only adds the rewriter on GPUs that Triton supports. A tiled scan computes one row per block, so scans with a dimension of at least 32768 also need at least 64 rows (`kMinRowsForLongScan`); otherwise the hierarchical scan of `AssociativeScanRewriter` is faster (crossover at 64 rows on H100 and 32 on B200). Shorter scans are faster with Triton at any batch size.

`CanTritonHandleScan` now rejects scans over any dimension other than the last one, for which the tiled Triton scan computes wrong results.

For a cumsum with an elementwise epilogue on f32[B, N], with B from 1 to 256 and N from 1024 to 262144, enabling the flag is never slower on H100 and B200. It is 1.05–2.9x (H100) and 1.06–2.8x (B200) faster for N < 32768, and up to 1.9x (H100) and 2.3x (B200) faster for N ≥ 32768 and B ≥ 64.

A top-p sampling mask (softmax, cumsum, compare and select) on f32[B, K] with B from 1 to 256 and K in {64, 128} compiles to a single Triton kernel: 1.3–1.5 µs instead of 3.3–4.5 µs on H100, and 2.5–3.1 µs instead of 5.9–8.4 µs on B200.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 982293610

display_title: Accept C99 complex exp results for an infinite real part in complex_unary_op_test.

head_commit.message:
Accept C99 complex exp results for an infinite real part in complex_unary_op_test.

llvm/llvm-project#232791 changed MLIR's ComplexToStandard lowering of
complex.exp, which the XLA CPU and GPU backends use, to return the C99 Annex G
values when the real part is infinite and the imaginary part is not finite:
exp(-inf + I*y) = 0 + 0*I and exp(+inf + I*y) = inf + NaN*I. Before, it
returned NaN + NaN*I, which is what complex_unary_op_samples.h expects.

ExpTest now skips those samples, and a new ExpInfRealNonFiniteImag test checks
these inputs (including y = NaN) and accepts either the old NaN + NaN*I result
or the C99 value. The test then passes with both old and new LLVM.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1005725749

display_title: Speed up single-threaded `GetMatchingPaths` and `FileSystem::IsDirectory`.

head_commit.message:
Speed up single-threaded `GetMatchingPaths` and `FileSystem::IsDirectory`.

In `GetMatchingPaths`, each `parent` directory in the queue has already been matched at previous levels, so we only need to match each `child` entry against the current segment's basename (`base_pattern`) rather than joining `parent` and `child` and re-matching the full path prefix. This avoids both re-evaluating earlier path components in `Match` and allocating joined path strings for non-matching entries.

Additionally, skip `GetChildren` when `base_pattern` contains no glob characters, avoid redundant `FileExists` calls on entries returned by `GetChildren`, reuse the `children` vector across iterations, and remove the redundant `FileExists` check before `Stat` in `FileSystem::IsDirectory`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1004366318

display_title: [Mosaic] Replace and erase original op before running downgrade rules in RunSerde.

head_commit.message:
[Mosaic] Replace and erase original op before running downgrade rules in RunSerde.

Previously, `RunSerde` passed `new_op` to `downgrade_rules` before replacing uses of `op` with `new_op` and erasing `op`. As a result, `new_op` had no uses during the downgrade rule (preventing downgrade rules from inserting post-processing ops that consume `new_op`), and setting `was_erased = true` in a downgrade rule would leave the unmangled `op` behind.

Replace `op`'s uses with `new_op` and erase `op` before invoking `downgrade_rules`, and split `SerdeRuleType` into `UpgradeRuleType` and `DowngradeRuleType` (removing the unused `bool&` parameter from downgrade rules).

display_title: Simplify tuple shapes in SPMD windowed einsum loops.

head_commit.message:
Simplify tuple shapes in SPMD windowed einsum loops.

Simplify the loop-state tuple shapes produced by `SpmdPartitioner` when sinking inputs or moving users into windowed einsum `kWhile` loops.

In `SinkInputNodesIntoWindowedDotGeneralLoopOnContractingDimensions` and `MoveUsersIntoWindowedDotGeneralLoopOnNonContractingDimensions`, replace the old loop-state entry in-place with the first new operand (or a scalar zero constant when sinking nullary-only inputs) and append any remaining new operands and outputs directly to the `kWhile` state tuple instead of packing them into a nested sub-tuple. This avoids nested tuples while preserving the canonical 5-element loop tuple indices `(0..4)`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1005696586

Add HloOpcode::kFma and mhlo.fma to XLA Core and MHLO.

Add `fma` ternary opcode to XLA HLO and MHLO to connect `stablehlo.fma` to XLA Core.

display_title: [XLA:BufferAssignment] Derive the OOM fallback chain from the algorithm, and split the last step into SPATIAL and TEMPORAL.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:BufferAssignment] Derive the OOM fallback chain from the algorithm, and split the last step into SPATIAL and TEMPORAL.

We have two flags: one enables fast buffer assignment with the fallback
(`--xla_tpu_buffer_assignment_enable_fast_merge_fallback`), and the other
specifies the buffer assignment algorithm (`--xla_tpu_buffer_assignment_algorithm`).

With the fallback enabled, the algorithm for AssignBuffersWithSequentialOrdering specified via `--xla_tpu_buffer_assignment_algorithm` is now the first one to try, and it defines the fallback chain. Previously, enabling the fallback led to not respecting `--xla_tpu_buffer_assignment_algorithm`.

The last step of the chain used DEFAULT (= BEST_OF_SPATIAL_TEMPORAL), which always runs the heap simulation twice. It is now split into SPATIAL and then TEMPORAL. **Since the fallback keeps the assignment with the lowest memory usage for each memory space, reaching TEMPORAL gives the same result as BEST_OF_SPATIAL_TEMPORAL, but TEMPORAL is skipped if SPATIAL already fits.**

The pairs below are (non-sequential, sequential) algorithms. Depending on `--xla_tpu_buffer_assignment_algorithm`:

* auto, FAST_MERGE: (FAST_MERGE, FAST_MERGE) → (FAST_MERGE, FAST_SPLIT) → (SPATIAL, SPATIAL) → (SPATIAL, TEMPORAL)
* FAST_SPLIT: (FAST_MERGE, FAST_SPLIT) → (SPATIAL, SPATIAL) → (SPATIAL, TEMPORAL)
* SPATIAL: (FAST_MERGE, SPATIAL) → (SPATIAL, SPATIAL) → (SPATIAL, TEMPORAL)
* TEMPORAL: (FAST_MERGE, TEMPORAL) → (SPATIAL, SPATIAL) → (SPATIAL, TEMPORAL)
* DEFAULT, BEST_OF_SPATIAL_TEMPORAL: (FAST_MERGE, X) → (SPATIAL, X)

`AssignmentAlgorithmForComputationsWithoutOrderingProto::DEFAULT` is renamed to `SPATIAL`: like the sequential SPATIAL, it assigns the biggest buffers first.

Only the memory spaces that exceed their memory limit (on TPU, HBM) are reassigned by the fallback steps. The other memory spaces (e.g. VMEM) keep the first assignment, as before.

**If the fallback flag is disabled, we respect the specified algorithm, and
nothing changes.**

display_title: [Mosaic] Replace and erase original op before running downgrade rules in RunSerde.

head_commit.message:
[Mosaic] Replace and erase original op before running downgrade rules in RunSerde.

Previously, `RunSerde` passed `new_op` to `downgrade_rules` before replacing uses of `op` with `new_op` and erasing `op`. As a result, `new_op` had no uses during the downgrade rule (preventing downgrade rules from inserting post-processing ops that consume `new_op`), and setting `was_erased = true` in a downgrade rule would leave the unmangled `op` behind.

Replace `op`'s uses with `new_op` and erase `op` before invoking `downgrade_rules`, and split `SerdeRuleType` into `UpgradeRuleType` and `DowngradeRuleType` (removing the unused `bool&` parameter from downgrade rules).

display_title: Simplify tuple shapes in SPMD windowed einsum loops.

head_commit.message:
Simplify tuple shapes in SPMD windowed einsum loops.

Simplify the loop-state tuple shapes produced by `SpmdPartitioner` when sinking inputs or moving users into windowed einsum `kWhile` loops.

In `SinkInputNodesIntoWindowedDotGeneralLoopOnContractingDimensions` and `MoveUsersIntoWindowedDotGeneralLoopOnNonContractingDimensions`, replace the old loop-state entry in-place with the first new operand (or a scalar zero constant when sinking nullary-only inputs) and append any remaining new operands and outputs directly to the `kWhile` state tuple instead of packing them into a nested sub-tuple. This avoids nested tuples while preserving the canonical 5-element loop tuple indices `(0..4)`.
